requirements.text: The application for approval of a type of ESA (the rear lamp electrical/electronic sub-assembly, e.g. LED PCB) with regard to electromagnetic compatibility shall be submitted by the vehicle manufacturer or by the manufacturer of the ESA.
The application for ESA type approval shall use the model information document shown in Annex 2B of UN R10.

The manufacturer may supplement the application with a report on tests already carried out; any such data provided may be used by the Type Approval Authority to draw up the communication form for type approval.

If the Technical Service responsible for the type approval test carries out the test itself, a sample of the ESA system representative of the type to be approved shall be provided, if necessary after discussion with the manufacturer on e.g. possible variations in layout, number of components and number of sensors; the Technical Service may select a further sample if it deems it necessary.
The ESA sample(s) submitted shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
Where applicable, any restrictions on use of the ESA shall be identified and included in Annexes 2B and/or 3B.

ESA brought to the market as replacement parts need no type approval provided they are obviously marked as a replacement part by an identification number and are identical to, and from the same manufacturer as, the corresponding original equipment.

Components sold as aftermarket equipment for installation in motor vehicles need no type approval if not related to immunity related functions (see paragraph 2.12); in this case the manufacturer shall issue a declaration that the ESA fulfils the requirements of UN R10, in particular the limits defined in paragraphs 6.5., 6.6., 6.7., 6.8. and 6.9.

Where an ESA (such as the rear lamp's LED light source/module electronics) is, or is part of, a light source, the applicant shall either (a) specify the approval number granted to this ESA according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128; or (b) provide a test report from a Technical Service designated by the Type Approval Authority stating that the ESA is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, Regulation No. 99 or Regulation No. 128.
The rear lamp, its vehicle installation and any ESA it contains shall be subject to approval in accordance with the approval provisions of UN R10 (paragraph 4, Approval).
Type approval under UN R10 shall follow the type approval procedures set out in paragraph 4.1, covering type approval of a vehicle and type approval of an ESA.
Vehicle type approval under UN R10 may be obtained through any of the alternative procedures in paragraph 4.1.1 (4.1.1.1 to 4.1.1.3), chosen at the discretion of the vehicle manufacturer.

A vehicle installation including the rear lamp may be type approved directly by following the provisions of paragraph 6 and, if applicable, paragraph 7 of UN R10; if this procedure is chosen by the vehicle manufacturer, no separate testing of electrical/electronic systems or ESAs is required.

A vehicle manufacturer may obtain vehicle approval by testing of individual ESAs by demonstrating to the Type Approval Authority that all relevant electrical/electronic systems or ESAs (see paragraph 3.1.3 of UN R10), such as the rear lamp's electronics, have been approved in accordance with this Regulation and installed in accordance with any conditions attached thereto.
A manufacturer may obtain approval according to UN R10 if the vehicle has no equipment of the type that is subject to immunity or emission tests; such approvals do not require testing.

Type approval of an ESA (such as the rear lamp's electronics) may be granted either for fitting to any vehicle type (component approval) or to a specific vehicle type or types requested by the ESA manufacturer (separate technical unit approval).

Where the rear lamp's ESAs (e.g. electronic control gear or LED electronics) are intentional RF transmitters and have not received type approval in conjunction with a vehicle manufacturer, they shall be supplied with suitable installation guidelines (UN R10 para 4.1.3).
Type approval under UN R10 shall be granted in accordance with the provisions of paragraph 4.2 (Granting of type approval), covering the vehicle (4.2.1) and the ESA (4.2.2).
The provisions for granting type approval to a vehicle in respect of electromagnetic compatibility, as set out in paragraphs 4.2.1.1 and 4.2.1.2 of UN R10, shall be applied.
Vehicle type approval shall be granted if the representative vehicle fulfils the requirements of paragraph 6 and, if applicable, paragraph 7 of UN R10.
The communication form for vehicle type approval shall follow the model contained in Annex 3A of UN R10.
The provisions for granting type approval to an ESA (such as the rear lamp's electronic components), as set out in paragraphs 4.2.2.1 and 4.2.2.2 of UN R10, shall be applied.
ESA type approval shall be granted if the representative ESA system(s) fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6 and, if applicable, paragraph 7 of UN R10.
The communication form for ESA type approval shall follow the model contained in Annex 3B of UN R10.

To draw up the communication forms referred to in paragraphs 4.2.1.2. or 4.2.2.2. of UN R10, the Type Approval Authority of the Contracting Party granting the approval may use a report prepared or approved by a recognized laboratory or one prepared in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.

Where an ESA (e.g. the rear lamp electronics) is (part of) a light source and the documentation specified in paragraph 3.2.10. of UN R10 is missing, approval of this ESA according to Regulation No. 10 shall not be granted.

Approval or refusal of approval of a vehicle type or ESA type under UN R10 shall be notified to the Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation on a form conforming to the model in Annex 3A or 3B, accompanied by photographs and/or diagrams or drawings on an appropriate scale supplied by the applicant, in a format not larger than A4 (210 x 297 mm) or folded to those dimensions.
The vehicle or ESA (including the rear lamp electronics) shall comply with the marking provisions of paragraph 5 of UN R10 (Markings).
An approval number shall be assigned to each vehicle type or ESA type approved in accordance with UN R10, in accordance with Schedule 4 of the 1958 Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
The presence of the approval markings shall comply with paragraph 5.2 of UN R10, as specified for vehicles (5.2.1) and for electrical/electronic sub-assemblies (5.2.2).
For a vehicle, an approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 of UN R10 shall be affixed to every vehicle conforming to a type approved under this Regulation.

For an electrical/electronic sub-assembly (ESA), an approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 of UN R10 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under this Regulation; no marking is required for electrical/electronic systems built into vehicles which are approved as units.

An international approval mark shall be affixed, in a conspicuous and easily accessible place specified on the approval communication form, on each vehicle conforming to the type approved under UN R10; the mark shall comprise the elements specified in paragraphs 5.3.1 and 5.3.2.

The approval mark on each vehicle shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval (distinguishing numbers of the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement are reproduced in Annex 3 to Consolidated Resolution R.E.3, ECE/TRANS/WP.29/78/Rev.6).
The approval mark shall comprise the number of UN R10, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, placed to the right of the circle specified in paragraph 5.3.1.
The type approval mark shall be consistent with the example shown in Annex 1 to UN R10.
Markings on ESAs in conformity with paragraph 5.3 need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle.
The specifications of paragraph 6 of UN R10 apply to vehicles and ESAs in configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.
The general specifications of paragraph 6.1 of UN R10 shall be met for configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted so as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.

The vehicle, with its electrical/electronic systems or ESAs (including the rear lamp), shall be designed, constructed and fitted to comply with UN R10 in normal conditions of use; a vehicle shall be tested for radiated emissions and for immunity to radiated disturbances; no tests for conducted emissions or immunity to conducted disturbances are required for vehicle type approval.

The vehicle and its electrical/electronic systems or ESAs shall be designed, constructed and fitted to comply with UN R10 in normal conditions of use; ESAs (such as the rear lamp's LED electronics) shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

Before testing, the Technical Service shall prepare a test plan with the manufacturer containing at least mode of operation, stimulated function(s), monitored function(s), pass/fail criterion(criteria) and intended emissions; depending on the intended operating conditions of the propulsion system, the plan shall define the minimum number of steady state operating conditions selectable by the driver or control system; test conditions shall consider multiple propulsion system operating strategies activated permanently by the driver or vehicle control system and shall be based on the documentation in Annexes 2A and 2B (e.g. risk analysis).
For configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid, the vehicle shall comply with the specifications concerning broadband electromagnetic radiation from vehicles.

The electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the method described in Annex 4; the method of measurement shall be defined by the vehicle manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.
The vehicle shall comply with the broadband type approval limits for vehicles specified in paragraph 6.2.2 and its sub-paragraphs.

If measured using the Annex 4 method with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, broadband emissions shall not exceed 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, the limit increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 2 to the Regulation.
Above 75 MHz the broadband limit shall follow the logarithmic increase shown in Appendix 2 to UN R10; in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band the limit shall remain constant at 43 dB microvolts/m.

When vehicle broadband emissions are measured per Annex 4 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the limits shall be 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band and 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, rising logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3 of the Regulation; in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band the limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the vehicle broadband type approval limits.
The vehicle shall comply with the specifications concerning narrowband electromagnetic radiation from vehicles, in configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.

The electromagnetic radiation generated by the vehicle representative of its type shall be measured using the narrowband method described in Annex 5, with the measurement conditions defined by the vehicle manufacturer in accordance with the Technical Service.
The vehicle shall comply with the vehicle narrowband type approval limits specified in paragraphs 6.3.2.1 to 6.3.2.3.

When vehicle narrowband emissions are measured per Annex 5 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the limits shall be 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz band and 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz band.

When vehicle narrowband emissions are measured per Annex 5 at a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the limits shall be 38 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz band and 45 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured narrowband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the narrowband type approval limit.

Per UN R10 para 6.4, the vehicle (with the rear lamp installed), in configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid, shall comply with the specifications concerning immunity of vehicles to electromagnetic radiation.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the vehicle representative of its type shall be tested by the method described in Annex 6 of UN R10.
The vehicle shall meet the vehicle immunity type approval limits specified in UN R10 para 6.4.2 (paras 6.4.2.1 and 6.4.2.2) for immunity to electromagnetic radiation.

If tested per Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, field strength shall be 30 V/m over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz band and at least 25 V/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz band, and 10 V/m over 90 per cent of the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band and at least 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz band; if tested per Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, current shall be 60 mA over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz band and at least 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz band.

The vehicle representative of its type shall be considered compliant with immunity requirements only if, during the tests per Annex 6, there is no degradation of performance of the "immunity related functions" according to paragraph 2.1 of Annex 6.

Electronic sub-assemblies (ESAs), such as the rear lamp's LED electronics on PCB, shall comply with the specification concerning broadband electromagnetic interference generated by ESAs per UN R10 para 6.5, in configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7 of UN R10.
The ESA shall meet the broadband type approval limits specified in UN R10 para 6.5.2 for electromagnetic interference generated by ESAs.

If ESA broadband electromagnetic radiation is measured using the method in Annex 7, the limits shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz) as shown in Appendix 6, and constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The ESA (electronic LED rear lamp assembly) shall comply with the specifications concerning narrowband electromagnetic interference generated by ESAs, in configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8 (narrowband method of measurement).
The ESA shall meet the ESA narrowband type approval limits specified in paragraph 6.6.2 (sub-paragraphs 6.6.2.1 and 6.6.2.2).

If ESA narrowband measurements are made using the method in Annex 8, the limits shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz) as shown in Appendix 7, and constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The ESA shall comply with the specifications concerning the emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines, in configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA (the rear lamp electronics) on 12/24 V supply lines, for an ESA representative of its type, shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, for the levels given in Table 1.

Transient conducted emission pulses of the ESA shall not exceed the maximum allowed pulse amplitudes of Table 1: for vehicles with 12 V systems, positive pulses +75 V and negative pulses -100 V; for vehicles with 24 V systems, positive pulses +150 V and negative pulses -450 V.
The ESA shall meet the specifications concerning immunity of ESAs to electromagnetic radiation, in configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
The ESA shall comply with the ESA immunity type approval limits for electromagnetic radiation immunity as specified in paragraph 6.8.2 and its subparagraphs.

The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) described in Annex 9, with test severity over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band as per Table 2a, and the minimum test level over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band as per Table 2b. Table 2a (below 2 GHz): stripline 20-400 MHz 60 V/m; TEM cell 20-200 MHz 75 V/m; BCI 20-400 MHz 60 mA; ALSE 80-2,000 MHz 30 V/m; reverberation chamber LUF-2,000 MHz 21 V/m; above 2 GHz: ALSE 2,000-6,000 MHz 10 V/m, reverberation chamber 2,000-6,000 MHz 7 V/m, other methods not applicable. Table 2b (minimum): stripline 50 V/m; TEM cell 62.5 V/m; BCI 50 mA; ALSE 25 V/m; reverberation chamber 18 V/m; above 2 GHz: ALSE 8 V/m, reverberation chamber 6 V/m, other methods not applicable.

The ESA representative of its type shall be considered compliant with the immunity requirements if, during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there is no degradation of performance of immunity related functions.

The ESA shall meet the specifications concerning immunity of ESAs to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines, in configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.

Immunity of the ESA (representative of the type) to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested per ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, at the test levels of Tables 3a and 3b. Starting profile: 10 pulses, level II (12 V and 24 V), tested per the functional status classification of ISO 16750-1; status B for ESA related to immunity related functions that shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other ESA related to immunity related functions, D for ESA not related to immunity related functions. Pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b shall be applied with FPSC per ISO 7637-1: pulse 1 -75 V (12 V)/-450 V (24 V), 500 pulses, FPSC III for related and III for not related; pulse 2a +37 V/+37 V, 500 pulses, I and III; pulse 2b +10 V/+20 V, 10 pulses, II and III; pulse 3a -112 V/-150 V, 1 h, I and III; pulse 3b +75 V/+150 V, 1 h, I and III. The starting profile applies only to ESAs installable in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor.
The exceptions set out in paragraph 6.10 (6.10.1 to 6.10.6) shall apply to specifications in configurations other than REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid.

Where a vehicle or electrical/electronic system or ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2 or 6.6.2 and with Annexes 5 and 8.

Vehicles that do not have electrical/electronic systems with immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.4 and with Annex 6.
ESAs with no immunity related functions need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8 and with Annex 9.

Electrostatic discharge: for vehicles fitted with tyres, the body/chassis is considered an electrically isolated structure; significant electrostatic forces occur only at occupant entry or exit while the vehicle is stationary, so no type approval test for electrostatic discharge is deemed necessary.

Emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by ESAs on 12/24 V supply lines: ESAs that are not switched, contain no switches or do not include inductive load need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.

Loss of function of receivers during the immunity test, when the test signal is within the receiver bandwidth (RF exclusion band) specified for the specific radio service/product in the harmonized international EMC standard, does not necessarily lead to fail criteria.

RF transmitters shall be tested in the transmit mode; wanted emissions (e.g. from RF transmitting systems) within the necessary bandwidth and out-of-band emissions are disregarded for the purpose of UN R10; spurious emissions remain subject to UN R10 (applies to the rear lamp only if it contains an RF transmitter).

For the application of RF transmitter testing under UN R10 para 6.10.7, 'necessary bandwidth' shall be understood as, for a given class of emission, the width of the frequency band just sufficient to ensure transmission of information at the required rate and quality under specified conditions (ITU Radio Regulations Article 1, No. 1.152).

For the application of RF transmitter testing under UN R10 para 6.10.7, 'out-of-band emissions' shall be understood as emission on a frequency or frequencies immediately outside the necessary bandwidth resulting from the modulation process, excluding spurious emissions (ITU Radio Regulations Article 1, No. 1.144).

For the application of RF transmitter testing under UN R10 para 6.10.7, 'spurious emissions' shall be understood as emissions on a frequency or frequencies outside the necessary bandwidth, the level of which may be reduced without affecting the corresponding information transmission, including harmonic emissions, parasitic emissions, intermodulation products and frequency conversion products, but excluding out-of-band emissions (ITU Radio Regulations Article 1, No. 1.145); these are subject to UN R10.
For trolleybuses, the AC/DC mains portion of the vehicle propulsion system shall be excluded from UN R10; this exception is not relevant to an M1 passenger car rear lamp.

Additional specifications of UN R10 paragraph 7 shall be met in the configuration 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid' (relevant only where the vehicle with the rear lamp has such a charging mode).

The general specifications of UN R10 paragraph 7.1 shall be met for the configuration 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid' (relevant only where the vehicle with the rear lamp has such a charging mode).

A vehicle and its electrical/electronic systems or ESAs, including the LED rear lamp electronics, shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle, in configuration 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', complies with the requirements of UN R10.

A vehicle in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be tested for radiated emissions, immunity to radiated disturbances, conducted emissions and immunity to conducted disturbances, and the vehicle and its electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted to comply with UN R10 in that configuration.

For vehicle testing in charging mode, the artificial networks defined in Appendix 8 shall be used: Artificial networks (AN) for low voltage power supplies; High Voltage Artificial Networks (HV-AN) for DC power supplies; Direct Current charging Artificial Networks (DC-charging-AN) for DC power supplies; Artificial Mains Networks (AMN) for AC power mains; Asymmetric Artificial Networks (AAN) for signal/control port lines and/or wired network port lines.

For an ESA powered by LV, a 5 µH / 50 Ω AN as defined in Figure 1 shall be used; the AN(s) shall be mounted directly on the ground plane with the grounding connection bonded to the ground plane; measurement ports shall be terminated with a 50 Ω load; the AN impedance ZPB (tolerance ±20 %) in the frequency range 0,1 MHz to 100 MHz shall be as shown in Figure 2, measured between terminals P and B with a 50 Ω load on the measurement port and terminals A and B short circuited.

The 5 µH AN shall correspond to the example schematic of Figure 1: L1 5 µH, C1 0,1 µF, C2 1 µF (default value), R1 1 kΩ, with port A to the power supply, port P to the ESA, B as ground and MEP as the measuring port.

For a signal/control port with control pilot, a special AAN as defined in Figure 11 shall be used, providing a common mode impedance of 150 Ω ± 20 Ω (150 kHz to 30 MHz) on the control pilot line (between A and B/D), typically combined with a communication simulation; the inductance and capacitance values shall not induce any malfunction of communication between vehicle and charging station and may be adapted to ensure proper communication; if control pilot communication is emulated and the AAN prevents proper communication, no AAN should be used.

The AAN for the pilot line shall follow the example circuit of Figure 11: C1 1,1 nF, L1 100 µH, R1 150 Ω, with the AAN (1) between the vehicle (2) and the charging station (3), control pilot line on the vehicle side (A), protective earth (B/D) and control pilot line on the charging station side (C).

Approval marks shall follow the examples of Annex 1 (Model A and Model B, see paragraph 5.2), with a = 6 mm min; a mark affixed to a vehicle or ESA shows the type has been approved with regard to electromagnetic compatibility in the Netherlands (E 4) pursuant to Regulation No. 10 under approval No. 07 2439, the number indicating approval under the 07 series of amendments; Model B shows approval pursuant to UN Regulations Nos. 10 and 33.

Where the approval mark combines UN Regulations Nos. 10 and 33, the approval numbers shall indicate that at the date of approval UN Regulation No. 10 included the 07 series of amendments and UN Regulation No. 33 was still in its original form.

The information document for type approval of a vehicle with respect to electromagnetic compatibility (UN R10 Annex 2A) shall be supplied in triplicate with a list of contents; drawings shall be at appropriate scale and in sufficient detail; paper submissions shall be on A4 size or in an A4 folder, while electronic submissions may be of any standard size; photographs, if any, shall show sufficient detail; if the systems, components or separate technical units have electronic controls, information concerning their performance shall be supplied (e.g. for the rear lamp LED PCB electronics).
The information document shall state the make (trade name of the manufacturer) of the vehicle (general information, item 1).
The information document shall state the type of the vehicle (general information, item 2).
The information document shall state the category of the vehicle (general information, item 3), e.g. M1 for a passenger car.
The information document shall state the name and address of the manufacturer and, if any, the name and address of the authorised representative (item 4).
The information document shall state the address(es) of the assembly plant(s) (item 5), under the heading general construction characteristics of the vehicle.
The information document shall include photograph(s) and/or drawing(s) of a representative vehicle (item 6).
The information document shall state the position and arrangement of the engine (item 7), under the heading power plant.
The type-approval information document (UN R10 Annex 2A, item 8) shall state the manufacturer's name and address.

The type-approval information document (UN R10 Annex 2A, items 9, 10a, 10b) shall state the manufacturer's engine code as marked on the engine; list the propulsion systems, auxiliary engines and components of the charging system; and list the modes of operation (selectable by the driver or the system) selected during the type approval test.

For a vehicle in configuration 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', the emission test setup shall follow the example setups in Figure 5 (5a-5h): vehicle under test on an insulating support, charging harness (including EVSE for charging mode 2), grounded AMN(s) or DC-charging-AN(s), power mains socket; for charging modes 3 or 4 with communication also optional grounded AAN(s), charging station (may be emulated), communication lines, communication module and power cable; for sockets located on the vehicle side or at the front/rear; the cable between the mains/supply and the AMN/DC-charging-AN need not be aligned in the same direction as the cable between the AMN/DC-charging-AN and the EV.
Radiated broadband electromagnetic emissions from electrical/electronic sub-assemblies (ESAs), such as the LED PCB of the rear lamp, shall be measured using the method of UN R10 Annex 7.
Annex 7 general provisions on measuring radiated broadband emissions from ESAs shall be applied (section 1 heading).

The Annex 7 test method may be applied to ESAs that may subsequently be fitted to vehicles complying with Annex 4, covering both (a) ESAs other than those involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid' and (b) ESAs involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid'.

Broadband electromagnetic emissions from ESAs (e.g. ignition systems, electric motor, onboard battery charging unit) shall be measured with the Annex 7 test method; unless otherwise stated in Annex 7, the test shall be performed according to CISPR 25.
The ESA shall be operated in the states specified in Annex 7 section 2 during the tests (ESA state during tests).

During the Annex 7 emission tests, the ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load; ESAs involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall be in charging mode; the traction battery SOC shall be kept between 20 per cent and 80 per cent of maximum SOC during the whole frequency range measurement (measurement may be split into sub-bands, discharging the battery before the next sub-band); if the test is not performed with a REESS, the ESA should be tested at rated current; if current consumption can be adjusted, it shall be set to at least 80 per cent of maximum rated charging/input current for AC charging, and for DC charging to at least 20 per cent of nominal value or a minimum of 16 A (if 20 per cent cannot be achieved in the test facility), unless another value is agreed with the type approval authorities.
The test arrangements for the Annex 7 ESA tests shall comply with the provisions of paragraph 3 (3.1 and 3.2 and sub-paragraphs).
For ESA other than those involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
For ESAs in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the test arrangement shall be according to Figure 2 of the appendix to Annex 7.

For ESAs in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid, the shielding configuration shall be according to the vehicle series configuration; generally all shielded High Voltage (HV) parts shall be properly connected with low impedance to ground (e.g. AN, cables, connectors); ESAs and loads shall be connected to ground; the external HV power supply shall be connected via feed-through-filtering.

For ESAs in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid, the ESA power supply lead shall be connected to the power supply through an HV-AN (for ESA with DC HV supply) and/or AMN (for ESA with AC supply); DC HV supply shall be applied via a 5 μH/50 Ω HV-AN (see Appendix 8, paragraph 2); AC supply shall be applied via a 50 μH/50 Ω AMN (see Appendix 8, paragraph 4).

For ESAs in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid, unless otherwise specified, the length of the LV harness and the HV harness parallel to the front edge of the ground plane shall be 1,500 mm (±75 mm); the total length of the test harness including the connector shall be 1,700 mm (+300/-0 mm); the distance between the LV harness and the HV harness shall be 100 mm (+100/-0 mm).
For ESAs in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid, all harnesses shall be placed on a non-conductive, low relative permittivity material (εr ≤ 1.4), at 50 mm (±5 mm) above the ground plane.

For ESAs tested in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" (test arrangement per Figure 2 of the appendix to Annex 7), shielded supply lines for HV+ and HV- and the three phase lines may be coaxial cables or in a common shield depending on the plug system used; the original HV-harness from the vehicle may optionally be used.

For ESAs tested in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" (Figure 2 of the appendix to Annex 7), unless otherwise specified, the ESA case shall be connected to the ground plane either directly or via a defined impedance.

For onboard chargers tested in configuration "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" (Figure 2 of the appendix to Annex 7), the AC/DC power lines shall be placed furthest from the antenna (behind the LV and HV harness), with a distance between the AC/DC power lines and the closest harness (LV or HV) of 100 mm (+100/-0 mm).

As an alternative to an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE), an open area test site (OATS) complying with the requirements of CISPR 16-1-4 may be used as the measuring location (see Figure 1 of the appendix to Annex 7).

Ambient: to ensure no extraneous noise or signal materially affects the measurement, ambient measurements shall be taken before or after the main test; the extraneous noise or signal shall be at least 6 dB below the interference limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1. of UN R10, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
The test requirements of Annex 7 (radiated broadband emission test) shall be met as set out in the following paragraphs 4.1 and 4.2.
The emission limits shall apply throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or on an open area test site (OATS).

Measurements may be performed with either quasi-peak or peak detectors; the limits in paragraphs 6.5. and 7.10. of UN R10 are for quasi-peak detectors, and if peak detectors are used a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.

Annex 7 para 4.3 (test requirements): Radiated emission measurements on the ESA (rear lamp electronics) shall be performed with a spectrum analyser or a scanning receiver using the parameters defined in Table 1 and Table 2; spectrum analysers and FFT-based instruments meeting CISPR 16-1-1 may be used for conformity measurements; FFT-based instruments shall continuously record and evaluate the signal during the measurement time, with a minimum measurement time of 1 s per analysis frequency band (real-time mode).

The test method(s) described in UN R10 Annex 9 shall be applied to the rear lamp as an ESA.

Any extraneous equipment required to operate the ESA under test shall not be in place during the calibration phase, and no extraneous equipment shall be closer than 1 m from the reference point during calibration.

The ESA shall meet the general test requirements of UN R10 Annex 9 paragraph 3, covering frequency range and dwell times, test intervals, and verification of failures.

For type approval of the lamp, all definitions given in the latest series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 48 in force at the time of application for type approval shall apply, unless otherwise specified in UN R148 or in the pertinent installation UN Regulations Nos. 53, 74 and 86.

Lamps shall be treated as 'lamps of different types' when they differ in essential respects: (a) trade name or mark (same mark by different manufacturers = different types; same manufacturer differing only by trade name or mark = same type); (b) characteristics of the optical system (intensity levels, light distribution angles, inclusion or elimination of components altering optical effects by reflection, refraction, absorption and/or deformation during operation, etc.); (c) category or categories of light source(s) and/or specific identification code(s) of light source module(s); (d) lamp category, if any; (e) variable intensity control, if any; (f) sequential activation of light sources, if any. Direction indicators activated in different modes without modification of optical characteristics are not of different types; a change of colour of the light source or of any filter is not a change of type; use of LED substitute light source(s) is not a change of type, however paragraph 4.8.1.6 applies.
Any component 'being part of the lamp' shall be either physically included in the lamp body, or external (separated or not) and declared by the applicant as part of the lamp system.
The rear lamp shall comply with the administrative provisions of UN R148 paragraph 3 governing the type approval application and its accompanying documentation.
The application for approval of the rear lamp type shall be made and handled in accordance with UN R148 paragraph 3.1 (Application for approval).
The application for type approval of the rear lamp shall be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark or by his duly accredited representative.

For a lamp differing only by trade name or mark from an approved type, the application shall include two samples bearing the new trade name or mark, or equivalent documentation.

For a lamp with variable intensity, the application for approval shall be accompanied by a concise description of the variable intensity control, an arrangement diagram and a specification of the characteristics of the system covering the entire range of intensity.

A separate approval shall be obtained for each lamp listed in paragraph 1 of UN R148.

Where two or more lamps (e.g. rear position, stop, reversing lamp and retro-reflector in one housing) form a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, approval may be granted only if each lamp satisfies the provisions of UN R148 or of another Regulation; any lamp not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of such a unit.

Approval shall be granted if the lamp type submitted under paragraph 3.1 meets the requirements of UN R148; all devices of an interdependent lamp system shall be submitted for type approval by the same applicant.

Notice of approval, extension, refusal or withdrawal of approval, or production definitely discontinued, for a lamp type under UN R148 shall be communicated to the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying this Regulation, using a form conforming to the model in Annex 1.

An approval number shall be assigned to each approved lamp type and indicated for each lamp in the Annex 1 communication form; a Contracting Party may assign the same approval number to light-signalling devices or systems incorporating several lamps, but shall not assign the same number to another lamp type of the same function.
The lamp shall carry the symbols identifying the light signalling lamp (function) for which type approval has been granted.

The approval marking shall use the symbols of Table 1 for each function: rear position lamp steady R1 or variable R2 (para 5.2); stop lamp steady S1 or variable S2 (para 5.5); reversing lamp AR (letters A and R may be mingled, para 5.8); other listed functions only if fitted (e.g. rear fog lamp F1/F2, para 5.9; rear direction indicator 2a/2b, para 5.6; rear registration plate lamp L, para 5.11; rear end-outline marker RM1/RM2, para 5.2; central high-mounted stop lamp S3/S4, para 5.5; others per Table 1).

The approval shall indicate the series of amendments (00 or 01) and the change index for each specific lamp function per Table 2 (change index 0 or 1 for rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp and other listed functions); the reversing projector is not available for type approval under series 00 (dash) and has index 0 under series 01.
The lamp shall bear the approval marking and other markings as required by paragraph 3.3 of UN R148.

General provisions for approval marking and other markings (UN R148 para 3.3.1): the rear lamp shall comply with the general provisions on approval marking and other markings set out in paragraphs 3.3.1.1 to 3.3.1.2.

Every device belonging to an approved type, including each rear lamp function device, shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the device (approval marking and other markings) shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking shall have a size parameter "a" of at least 5 mm (Figure I); examples of the arrangement of the markings are shown in Annex 7.
The approval marking of the lamp shall consist of the elements specified in paragraphs 3.3.2.1 to 3.3.2.3.
The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number that is part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2, placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamps (functions of the rear lamp) as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.

The approval marking, which shall consist of the elements listed in paragraph 3.3.2, shall include the number of UN Regulation No. 148 followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
The approval marking shall include, if applicable, the additional symbol(s) specified in paragraphs 3.3.2.5.1 to 3.3.2.5.3.

On lamps which cannot be mounted indiscriminately on either side of the vehicle, the approval marking shall include, as an additional symbol, a horizontal arrow showing the position in which the lamp is to be mounted.

The mounting-position horizontal arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle for: (a) direction indicators of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12; (b) front or rear position lamps and front or rear end-outline marker lamps; (c) reversing lamps, in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
The mounting-position horizontal arrow shall be directed towards the front of the vehicle in the case of direction indicators of categories 5 and 6 and combined parking lamps.
For direction indicators of category 6, an indication 'R' or 'L' shall be shown on the lamp, indicating the right or left side of the vehicle (applicable only if such a direction indicator is used).

If applicable, the following shall be marked to the right of the symbol mentioned in paragraph 3.2.4: (a) the additional letter 'D' on lamps which may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps; (b) the additional letter 'Y' on lamps which are used as part of an interdependent lamp system.
On lamps with reduced light distribution (see paragraph 1.1 of Annex 3), the approval marking shall include a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
The rear lamp shall comply with the marking requirements of paragraph 3.3.3 (approval marking and other markings) of UN R148, as set out in paragraphs 3.3.3.1 to 3.3.3.6.
The rear lamp shall bear the approval marking.
The rear lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

Except for lamps with non-replaceable light sources, the lamp shall be marked with (a) the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed; and (b) where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), also the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).

The lamp shall be marked with its rated voltage(s) (6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or the range of voltage where it has an electronic light source control gear; and/or a variable luminous intensity control; and/or a secondary operating mode; and/or non-replaceable light sources.

Where replaceable light source module(s) are used, the following markings shall be borne. (a) On the light source module(s): (i) the trade name or mark of the applicant; (ii) the specific identification code of the module, comprising the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.2.1 (see 3.3.2.1.1 for additional symbols); (iii) the rated voltage(s) or range of voltage. (b) On the lamp: the module identification code and the rated voltage(s) or range of voltage.

Where several non-identical light source modules are used, the module identification code (MD followed by the approval mark without the circle per 3.3.2.1, being a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the approving country) shall be followed by additional symbols or characters; the approval mark need not be the same as that on the lamp in which the module is used, but both marks shall be from the same applicant; the module shall show the rated voltage(s) or range of voltage; the lamp shall bear the module's specific identification code per 3.3.3.5(a)(ii) and the rated voltage(s) or range of voltage.

Where an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, it shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking and other markings of the lamp (UN R148 para 3.3) shall be placed in accordance with the marking location provisions of paragraph 3.3.4 (sub-paragraphs 3.3.4.1 to 3.3.4.7).
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

In any case, the approval marking and the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
Where an outer lens is used for several devices bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5.(b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.
The markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3.(a), 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. and 3.3.3.6. do not need to fulfil the visibility requirements of paragraph 3.3.4.2.

Approval marking and other markings for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (e.g. the rear lamp combining rear position, stop, reversing lamp and retro-reflector in one housing) shall comply with the provisions of UN R148 para 3.3.5 on their approval marking.

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps have been found to comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number may be affixed; this marking may be located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided that the conditions of paras 3.3.5.1.1 and 3.3.5.1.2 are met.
The single approval mark of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be visible after their installation.

The single approval mark shall be located such that no part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light can be removed without at the same time removing the approval mark.

The size of the components of a single approval mark on grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

Approval marking arrangements for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, including all the additional symbols mentioned above, shall be consistent with the examples given in Annex 7 of UN R148.
Modifications of a type of lamp for motor vehicles and their trailers, and extension of approval, shall be handled in accordance with the administrative provisions of UN R148 para 3.4.

Every modification of a type of lamp shall be notified to the Type Approval Authority which approved the type; the Authority may then decide on the follow-up options listed in the subsequent sub-paragraphs.

Where a type of lamp is modified and the modification is notified to the Type Approval Authority that approved the type, the Authority may consider that the modifications are unlikely to have an appreciable adverse effect and that the lamp in any case still complies with the requirements.

Where a type of lamp is modified and the modification is notified to the Type Approval Authority that approved the type, the Authority may instead require a further test report from the technical service responsible for conducting the tests.

Confirmation or refusal of approval for a modification or extension of a type of lamp, specifying the alterations, shall be communicated by the procedure specified in paragraph 3.2.3.1 to the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying this Regulation.

The Type Approval Authority issuing an extension of approval shall assign a series number to the extension and inform the other Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying the UN Regulation under which approval was granted, by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.
Conformity of production procedures shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), together with the requirements set forth in paragraph 6.
Penalties for non-conformity of production shall apply as specified in paragraphs 3.6.1 and 3.6.2 (heading clause for withdrawal of approval and notification of withdrawal).
The approval granted may be withdrawn if the requirements of this Regulation are not met.

If a Contracting Party to the 1958 Agreement applying this Regulation withdraws an approval it has previously granted, it shall forthwith notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.

If the holder of the approval completely ceases to manufacture a lamp approved under UN R148 (production definitively discontinued), the holder shall inform the authority which granted the approval; upon receiving the communication, that authority shall inform the other Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying this Regulation by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.

Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying UN R148 shall communicate to the United Nations Secretariat the names and addresses of the Technical Services responsible for conducting approval tests and of the Type Approval Authorities which grant approval and to which forms certifying approval, extension, refusal, withdrawal of approval, or definitive discontinuation of production issued in other countries are to be sent.

Remarks on colours and particular devices for end-outline marker lamps and parking lamps: Contracting Parties to which UN R148 is annexed are not precluded by Article 3 of the Agreement from prohibiting, for lamps installed on vehicles registered by them, certain colours provided for in this Regulation, or from prohibiting, for all or certain categories of vehicles registered by them, stop lamps having only steady luminous intensity.
General technical requirements (section heading): the lamp submitted for approval shall meet the general technical requirements of paragraph 4 of UN R148, comprising paragraphs 4.1 to 4.4.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4 and 5 of UN R148.

The requirements of sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and the Annexes referenced therein) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, in their series of amendments in force at the time of application for lamp type approval, shall apply; the requirements pertinent to each lamp and to the vehicle category/ies on which it is intended to be installed shall be applied where verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

Lamps shall be designed and constructed so that in normal conditions of use, notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN R148.

Independent and interdependent lamps (heading): the lamp, including the rear lamp's combined functions in a single housing, shall comply with the provisions on independent and interdependent lamps set out under paragraph 4.4 of UN R148.

An assembly of two independent lamps type approved as a lamp marked "D" shall be applicable only to front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps.

An interdependent lamp system type approved as lamps marked "Y" shall be applicable only to front and rear position lamps, stop lamps, front and rear end-outline marker lamps, daytime running lamps and direction indicator lamps.

Lamps shall comply with the provisions of UN R148 para 4.5 for lamps as such or grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated (applicable to the rear lamp combining several functions in one housing).
Lamps approved as front or rear position lamps are deemed to be also approved as end-outline marker lamps.
Front and rear position lamps which are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated may also be used as end-outline marker lamps.

Position lamps or daytime running lamps reciprocally incorporated with another function, using a common light source and designed to operate permanently with an additional system regulating the intensity of the emitted light, are permitted.

For a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp (with common light source and intensity regulation system per 4.5.3), these functions shall either (a) be provided by multiple light sources (for instance a double filament light source); or (b) be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure of the lamps; in either case a note shall be made in the communication document.

If a front position lamp incorporates one or more infrared radiation generators, its photometric and colour requirements shall be met both with and without operation of the infrared radiation generator(s).

On request of the applicant, the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function) may incorporate only one manufacturer logo made of transparent or non-transparent components, provided all requirements for the specific function are fulfilled and: (a) irrespective of paragraph 3.3 marking requirements, only the brand-name logo of the vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer is allowed, confirmed by an applicant statement (para 3.1.2.2.(f)); (b) the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (transparent and non-transparent components) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2; (c) notwithstanding para 5.5.2 of UN R48, the logo light emitting surface need not be symmetrical by itself; (d) stop lamps, direction indicator lamps and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.
The lamp shall comply with the general technical failure provisions of paragraph 4.6 of UN R148.
For failure of a single lamp containing more than one light source, the lamp shall comply with the provisions of paragraph 4.6.1 of UN R148.
In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that failure of any one causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one of the following shall apply: (a) the light intensity complies with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution in Annex 3, and the maximum intensities are not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated; or (b) a signal for activation of a failure tell-tale as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN R48 is produced, in which case a note in the communication form states that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

For daytime running lamps (applicable only if the lamp includes this function), instead of para 4.6.1.2 and in addition to para 4.6.1.1, in case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, at least one shall apply: (a) the light intensity at the standard light distribution points defined in paragraph 2.2 of Annex 3 is at least 80 per cent of the minimum intensity required; or (b) a failure tell-tale signal as indicated in paragraph 6.19.8 of UN R48 is produced, with a note in the communication form that the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

For direction-indicator lamps of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 11, 11a, 11b, 11c and 12 (applicable only if the lamp includes this function), instead of para 4.6.1.2 and in addition to para 4.6.1.1, the tell-tale of para 6.5.8 of R48 or para 6.3.8 of R53 shall be activated based on option (a), (b) or (c), notwithstanding para 4.6: (a) any one light source has failed; (b) for a lamp designed for only two light sources, the intensity in the axis of reference is less than 50 per cent of the minimum required; (c) as a consequence of failure of one or more light sources, the intensity in one of the directions of para 2.1 of Annex 3 is less than the minimum required: (i) H=0°, V=0°; (ii) H=20° outwards, V=+5°; (iii) H=10° inwards, V=0°.
The requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.2 do not apply to rear registration plate lamps (relevant only if such a lamp is included); the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1 remain applicable.

For stop lamps and position lamps of vehicles of category L, the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.2.(b) do not apply; the requirements of paragraph 4.6.1.1. and paragraph 4.6.1.2.(a) (failure of a single lamp containing more than one light source) still apply.

In case of failure of the variable intensity control of (a) a rear position lamp category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1; (b) a rear end-outline marker lamp category RM2 emitting more than the maximum of RM1; (c) a stop lamp category S2 emitting more than the maximum of S1; (d) a stop lamp category S4 emitting more than the maximum of S3; (e) a direction indicator category 2b emitting more than the maximum of 2a; (f) a rear fog lamp category F2 emitting more than the maximum of F1, the requirements of steady luminous intensity of the respective category shall be fulfilled automatically.
The lamp shall comply with the provisions with regard to light sources set out in paragraph 4.7 (use of light sources and general requirements with regard to light sources).

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).

The lamp shall comply with the general requirements with regard to light sources set out in paragraph 4.7.2 (restricted light source use, replaceable light source fixing and holders, and electromagnetic disturbance).

Where a light source category or type is restricted for use in lamps on vehicles in use and originally equipped with such lamps, the applicant for type approval of the lamp shall declare that the lamp is only intended for installation on those vehicles, and this shall be noted in the communication form.

In case of replaceable UN approved light source(s): (a) the lamp design shall be such that the light source(s) can be fixed in no other position but the correct one; (b) the light source holder shall conform to the characteristics given in IEC Publication 60061, applying the holder data sheet relevant to the prescribed light source category and, where a category of LED substitute light source is also prescribed, the holder data sheet relevant to that LED substitute category.

The light signalling device shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle (compliance with electromagnetic compatibility requirements is relevant to the vehicle type).

In case replaceable light source module(s) are used in the lamp, their design shall ensure that: (a) the module can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s); (b) it is tamperproof; (c) regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics located in the same lamp housing; (d) when the module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device are still met.
Test conditions and measurement methods specified in paragraph 4.8 of UN R148 shall be applied for the verification of the lamp's general technical requirements.
All photometric and colorimetric measurements of the lamp shall be made in accordance with the conditions of paragraph 4.8.1, using the measurement methods given in Annex 3.
In case replaceable UN approved light sources are used, all measurements shall be made using standard light sources as specified in R.E.5.

In case replaceable UN approved light source(s) are controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, the standard light source(s) used for measurements shall have a luminous flux that does not deviate more than 5 per cent from its reference/objective luminous flux value when test voltage is applied.
In case the lamp is equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements shall be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.

In case a lamp (function) uses light sources subject to more than one of the conditions of paragraph 4.8, photometric measurements shall be made separately for each applicable condition and all separate results shall be added together; the test laboratory may require the applicant to provide samples allowing the different light source(s) to be supplied separately.
During photometric measurements, stray reflections shall be avoided by appropriate masking.

Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one position or in a field of different positions, the photometric (and colorimetric) measurements shall be repeated for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.

Where, at the applicant's discretion, the lamp is also to be approved with LED substitute light source(s), all photometric and colorimetric measurements shall be repeated using the prescribed LED substitute light source(s).
Unless otherwise specified, intensities shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.

Where measurement results are challenged, measurements shall be carried out so as to meet the following requirements: distance of measurement, measuring equipment angular aperture, and tolerance on direction of observation (as specified in paras 4.8.1.8.1 to 4.8.1.8.3).
Where measurement results are challenged, the measurement distance shall be such that the law of the inverse of the square of the distance is applicable.
Where measurement results are challenged, the measuring equipment shall be such that the angular aperture of the receiver, viewed from the reference centre of the light, is between 10' and 1 degree.

Where measurement results are challenged, the intensity requirement for a particular direction of observation shall be deemed satisfied if it is met in a direction deviating by not more than one-quarter of a degree from the direction of observation.

The limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of a light-signalling lamp shall be determined; for category 5 and 6 direction indicators the limits of the light emitting surface shall be determined instead; this requirement does not apply to rear-registration plate illuminating lamps.

For a lamp intended to be mounted inside the vehicle, the sample plate(s) as supplied (para 3.1.2.8; several plates if different possibilities exist) shall be positioned in front of the lamp under test, in the geometrical position(s) described in the application drawing(s) (para 3.1.2.2), for all photometric and colorimetric measurements per Annex 3.
Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall be tested with the voltage supplied at the lamp of 6.75 V (6 Volt systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt systems) or 28 V (24 Volt systems).

For a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant; the test laboratory may require the electronic light source control gear or the variable intensity control.

For a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control: light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s) shall be operated as specified by the applicant; replaceable UN approved light source(s) shall be operated at the reference/objective luminous flux, or alternatively at a different luminous flux with proportional correction of the measured luminous intensities.

For lamps with multiple replaceable UN approved light sources, either operate them at a voltage or current setting such that the actual luminous fluxes do not deviate more than 5 per cent from the average luminous flux, with measured intensities corrected proportionally for the difference between average and applicable reference/objective luminous flux; or alternatively test using one light source in each lamp holder position operating at the reference/objective luminous flux and apply the sum of the measured luminous intensities for each direction.

The identification of the electronic light source control gear (if applicable) or variable intensity control (if applicable) and/or the voltage applied, including tolerances, shall be noted in the communication form in Annex 1.
Luminous intensities of the lamp shall be measured and assessed according to the test conditions and measurement methods of para 4.8.3 (heading for the luminous intensity requirements in 4.8.3.1).

Unless otherwise specified, the light intensity of each of the two samples supplied shall: (a) on the reference axis (HV) be not less than the minimum in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5; (b) in no direction where the lamp is visible exceed the maximum in that table; (c) outside the reference axis be not less than either the table minimum multiplied by the percentage given in the pertinent light distribution figure in Annex 3 for each direction, or the intensity value given in that figure for each direction; (d) within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2 be not less than the minimum in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5; the Annex 3 provisions on local variations of intensity shall be observed.

In addition to the intensity requirements of 4.8.3.1 (minimum on the HV reference axis and maximum in any visible direction per the pertinent function table in paragraph 5), to verify visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear required by UN R48, the applicant may request an additional test showing that in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard horizontally and -2.5° to +5° vertically the maximum intensity is not more than 2.5·10-1 cd; this test may take into account the influence of the vehicle body.

Where an assembly of two independent lamps type approved as lamps marked "D" with the same function is deemed a single lamp, it shall comply with the maximum intensity requirement when all lamps are lit together and with the minimum intensity requirement if either lamp has failed.

An interdependent lamp system shall meet the luminous intensity requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together; however (a) if the system providing the rear position lamp is partly on a fixed and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s), and the inboard geometric visibility requirement is deemed satisfied if they still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the light distribution field at all fixed positions; (b) if the system providing the rear direction indicator function is partly on fixed and partly on movable components, the specified lamp(s) shall meet geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions, except for lamps on vehicles where additional lamps are activated in any fixed open position to fulfil or complete the geometric visibility angle, provided those additional lamps satisfy all position, photometric and colorimetric requirements for direction indicator lamps on the movable component.

If variable intensity control is used, it shall not generate signals that cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5 or exceeding the respective steady maximum (as detailed in 4.8.3.4.1 and 4.8.3.4.2).
If variable intensity control is used, it shall not generate signals that cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.

If variable intensity control is used, it shall not generate signals causing luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 for the specific lamp: (a) for systems depending only on daytime and night-time conditions, under night-time conditions; (b) for other systems, under standard conditions (good visibility, meteorological optical range MOR > 2,000 m per WMO Guide to Meteorological Instruments and Methods of Observation, Sixth Edition, 1996, and a clean lens).

If a rear position lamp and/or rear end-outline marker lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp (steady or variable intensity), the ratio of the measured luminous intensities of the two lamps lit simultaneously to that of the position/end-outline marker lamp lit alone at its intensity should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by horizontal lines through ±5° V and vertical lines through ±10° H of the light distribution table; if one or both reciprocally incorporated lamps contain more than one light source and are considered a single lamp, the values considered are those obtained with all sources in operation.
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities shall be carried out according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted shall be measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, applying the test procedure of paragraph 4.8; outside this field no sharp variation of colour shall be observed; for lamps with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be checked separately for each light source technology according to the applicable provisions of paragraphs 4.8.1 and 4.8.2; the test laboratory may require the applicant to supply samples allowing the different light source(s) to be supplied separately.
The lamp shall comply with the specific technical requirements of paragraph 5 of UN R148 applicable to its functions.

Front position lamps (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamps (AM) shall comply with the specific technical requirements of paragraph 5.1 (applicable only if such functions are present in the product).

For front position lamps (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamps (AM), the light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 3 (applicable only if such functions are present).

Front position lamps and front end-outline marker lamps of categories A, MA or AM shall meet Table 3: minimum luminous intensity (4.8.3.1 (a)) 4.0·10^0 cd, maximum luminous intensity 1.40·10^2 cd (4.8.3.1 (b)), 7.0·10^1 cd for a single A lamp marked "D" (para 3.3.2.5.2); standard light distribution per Figure A3-I (4.8.3.1 (c)); angles of geometric visibility per Table A2-1 (4.8.3.1 (d)); minimum luminous intensity 5·10^-2 cd as given in Table 3.
For front position lamps (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamps (AM), the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility shall meet the values given in Table 3.
For front position lamps (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamps (AM), there are no requirements on the minimum or maximum area of apparent surface.

For front end-outline marker lamps (AM) only (applicable to the rear lamp only if such a lamp is fitted), the standard light distribution measurement may, at the applicant's request, be considered from the VV line to the outboard side only (UN R148 para 5.1.4).
For front position lamps (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamps (AM), no additional specific requirements apply (UN R148 para 5.1.5).
For front position lamps (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamps (AM), failure provisions shall comply with paragraph 4.6 of UN R148 (para 5.1.6).
The colour of light emitted by front position lamps (A, MA) and front end-outline marker lamps (AM) shall be white; the lamp identified by symbol MA may be amber (UN R148 para 5.1.7).

Heat resistance test (applicable to rear fog lamp and daytime running lamp functions, if present): the lamp shall be subjected to one hour of continuous operation following a 20-minute warm-up period, at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C; the light source shall be of the category specified for the lamp and supplied with a current at a voltage giving the specified average power at the corresponding test voltage; for lamps with non-replaceable light sources (filament and other), the test shall be made with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with paragraph 5.4.5 of this Regulation.

Where only the maximum power is specified, the test shall be carried out by regulating the voltage to obtain a power equal to 90 per cent of the specified power; the specified average or maximum power shall in all cases be chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which it reaches the highest value; for lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources the test conditions of paragraph 5.4.5. or 5.9.5. of UN R148 shall be applied.

In the case of light sources operated by an electronic control gear to obtain variable luminous intensity, the test (at the power specified in Annex 6 paragraph 2) shall be carried out under the conditions given at minimum 90 per cent of the higher luminous intensity.

After the lamp has been stabilized at ambient temperature following the heat resistance test, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification shall be perceptible; in case of doubt the intensity of light shall be measured according to paragraph 5 of UN R148 and the values shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.

Marking example 2 (Figure A7-II): for a combination of lamps approved under UN R148 and the UN Regulation for Road Illumination Devices (149R), the approval marking shall show each function (e.g. front position lamp A and front fog lamp F3), plastic lens symbol (PL) where applicable, country code (e.g. E2), approval number (e.g. 3223), and each Regulation number with its series of amendments (e.g. 148R 01 and 149R 01); for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps the marking is arranged per the examples, and the vertical and horizontal lines schematizing the lamp shape are not part of the approval marking.
Light sources used in the lamp shall be tested in accordance with the testing procedures with respect to light sources set out in Annex 8 of UN R148.
The rear lamp shall be tested in accordance with the general test requirements of UN R148 Annex 8 paragraph 1, covering the photometric measurement conditions in paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
For lamps (functions) using incandescent technology only, the luminous intensities measured after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For lamps (functions) using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only (e.g. the LED modules on PCB of this rear lamp), the test requirements of paragraphs 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 shall apply.

For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps using non-incandescent light sources, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements; the distribution after 1 and 10 minutes may be calculated from the distribution measured after photometric stability by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV (a) after 1 minute, (b) after 10 minutes, and (c) after photometric stability has occurred.

For all other non-incandescent lamps (e.g. rear position and stop lamps), the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements; direction indicator lamps shall be operated in flashing mode (f = 1.5 Hz, duty factor 50 per cent); the distribution after 1 min may be calculated from the distribution after 30 min or after photometric stabilization by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at HV after 1 min and either after 30 min or after photometric stabilization.
The rear lamp shall meet the additional test requirements of UN R148 Annex 8 paragraph 2.
