Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution shall, in addition to paragraph 1, be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1; the distributions at that time may be calculated from the distribution measured according to paragraph 1 by applying at each test point the ratio of luminous intensities measured at the reference coordinate of the lamp (function) under consideration.

Additional photometric checks shall be made at the times after switch ON and reference coordinates in Table A8-1: front and rear position lamp 4 s at HV; stop lamp 0.2 s at HV; reversing lamp 0.2 s at HV; and, where such functions are fitted, rear registration plate illumination 4 s at any measurement point given in Annex 3, direction indicator Cat 1, 2, 11, 12 0.2 s at HV, Cat 5, 6 0.2 s at H5, V0, end-outline marker 4 s at HV, rear fog 4 s at HV, parking 4 s at HV, daytime running 4 s at HV, side marker 4 s at HV; manoeuvring N.A.

Where a lamp (function) uses incandescent technology only, it shall be deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time (Table A8-1 timing, per Annex 8 para 2.1), if the luminous intensity values measured according to paragraph 1.1 are compliant.

Where a lamp (function) uses LED technology only, it shall be deemed to comply with the corresponding intensity requirements at all points in time (Table A8-1 timing, per Annex 8 para 2.1), if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 are compliant.

Where a lamp (function) uses any other light generating technology, its corresponding intensity requirements shall be tested and checked for compliance at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

Where a lamp (function) uses more than one light generating technology, its corresponding intensity requirements shall be tested following the strictest time requirements of paragraphs 2.1.1 to 2.1.3 for the combination of technologies and checked for compliance.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the corresponding minimum intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time, starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.

The rear retro-reflector (retro-reflector for motor vehicles, independent or combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight) shall be approved according to the applicable series of amendments of UN R150 (00 or 01) as per Table 2 and its change index (0 or 1); a dash in Table 2 means the device is not available for type approval under that series of amendments.
The retro-reflector shall carry the approval marking and other markings as specified in the administrative provisions of UN R150 paragraph 3.3.
The retro-reflector shall comply with the general provisions on approval marking and other markings of UN R150 paragraph 3.3.1.

Every device of an approved type (rear lamp incorporating the retro-reflective device) shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2, or alternatively for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The size of the approval marking shall conform to the value of "a" defined in Table 1; the arrangement of the markings shall be consistent with the examples shown in Annex 10.
The approval marking of the device shall consist of the elements specified in paragraphs 3.3.2.1 to 3.3.2.4.
The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted the approval.

The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number that is part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2, and this sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the retro-reflective device as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.

The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation (UN R150) followed by the letter "R" and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval.
Approval marking and other markings: the retro-reflective device shall be provided with a Unique Identifier (UI) as specified in paragraph 3.3.3 of UN R150.
The approval marking defined in paragraph 3.3.2 may be replaced by the Unique Identifier, if available; the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format shown in the example (Figure I).

The Unique Identifier marked on the retro-reflective device (Figure I) shall indicate that the type concerned has been approved and that the relevant type approval information can be accessed on the UN secure internet database using the identifier (example: 270650).
The retro-reflective device shall meet the marking requirements of paragraph 3.3.4 of UN R150 (trade name or mark of the applicant and the 'TOP' orientation markings, where applicable).
The retro-reflective device shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

Retro-reflective devices shall bear: for a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the word 'TOP' inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle(s) of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer; for retro-reflective marking material of Class C, D, E or F, an orientation mark 'TOP' on any marking material whose retro-reflective system is not omni-rotational; for retro-reflective marking plates of Class 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 whose retro-reflective system is not omni-rotational, the word 'TOP' inscribed horizontally on the part intended to be the highest part of the plate when mounted on the vehicle.
The approval marking, Unique Identifier and other markings on the retro-reflective device shall comply with the marking location requirements of paragraph 3.3.5 of UN R150.
The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings required by paragraph 3.3.4 shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.

Where retro-reflective marking material of Class C, D, E or F is used, the markings shall be positioned on the outside at least once: (a) on strips at a 0.5 m distance, or (b) on areas within 100 mm x 100 mm.
Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps in retroreflective devices shall comply with the approval marking provisions of paragraph 3.3.6 (subparagraphs 3.3.6.1 to 3.3.6.3).

Where grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps comply with the requirements of several UN Regulations, a single approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier may be affixed, located anywhere on the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, provided the conditions of 3.3.6.1.1 and 3.3.6.1.2 are met.
The single approval mark of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be visible after their installation.

No part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the four to six-digit sequential number or the Unique Identifier.

The size of the components of a single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Approval marking arrangements for grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps with all the additional symbols mentioned above shall follow the examples given in Annex 10 of UN R150.

Modifications of a type of retro-reflective device for motor vehicles and their trailers, and extension of approval, shall be handled in accordance with the administrative provisions of paragraph 3.4 of UN R150.

Every modification of the type of retro-reflective device (the rear retro-reflector of the lamp) shall be notified to the Type Approval Authority which approved the type; the Authority may then act as set out in paragraphs 3.4.1.1 and 3.4.1.2 (either consider the modification acceptable or require a further technical service report).

Where a modification of the retro-reflective device type is notified, the Type Approval Authority may consider that the modifications made are unlikely to have an appreciable adverse effect and that in any case the retro-reflective device still meets the requirements; the modified retro-reflector shall in that case still meet the requirements of UN R150.

Where a modification of the retro-reflective device type is notified, the Type Approval Authority may alternatively require a further report from the technical service responsible for conducting the tests; the manufacturer shall provide for such further testing and report if required.

Confirmation or refusal of approval for a modified retro-reflective device type, specifying the alterations, shall be communicated by the procedure specified in paragraph 3.2.2 to the Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying UN R150.

The Type Approval Authority issuing an extension of approval for a retro-reflective device shall assign a series number to the extension and inform the other Contracting Parties to the 1958 Agreement applying the UN Regulation under which approval was granted by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.

Conformity of production procedures for the retro-reflector shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the requirements of paragraphs 3.5.1 and 3.5.1.1.
Retro-reflectors approved under UN R150 shall be manufactured so as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4 and 5 of the Regulation.
The minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures set forth in Annex 2 of UN R150 shall be complied with for the retro-reflector.

For retro-reflectors approved under UN R150 (manufactured to conform to the approved type by meeting paragraphs 4 and 5), the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 3 shall be complied with.

Under the conformity of production procedures (1958 Agreement, Schedule 1, E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), the authority that granted type approval may at any time verify the conformity control methods applied in each production facility; the normal frequency of these verifications shall be once every two years.

Advance warning triangles approved under UN R150 shall be manufactured to conform to the approved type; compliance with the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 shall be verified as specified in the following sub-paragraphs (conformity of production).

For advance warning triangles, the stability in time of the optical properties and colour of retro-reflecting optical units of triangles conforming to an approved type and in use shall additionally be verified; in the event of a systematic deficiency (an approved type failing to meet the requirements of paragraph 5) in units in use, approval may be withdrawn.
Any retro-reflective marking material approved under UN R150 shall be manufactured to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5 (conformity of production).

For retro-reflective marking material, conformity of production shall not be contested if the mean value of the photometric measurements of five specimens taken at random deviates unfavourably by not more than 20 per cent from the prescribed values given in paragraphs 4 and 5.

For retro-reflective marking material, conformity of production shall not be contested if the mean value of the colorimetric properties of five specimens taken at random meets the specifications of paragraphs 4 and 5, judged by visual inspection.

For retro-reflective marking material, the authority that granted type approval may at any time verify the conformity control methods applied in each production facility; the normal frequency of these verifications shall be once every two years.

Conformity of production (UN R150 para 3.5, procedures per 1958 Agreement Schedule 1, E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3): any retro-reflective marking plates approved to this Regulation shall be manufactured to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of paragraphs 4. and 5.; for resistance to external agents, only paragraph 5.7.6.1. applies.
For retro-reflective marking plates, the minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures set forth in Annex 2 to UN R150 shall be complied with.
For retro-reflective marking plates, the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector set forth in Annex 3 to UN R150 shall be complied with.

The type approval authority may at any time verify the conformity control methods applied in each production facility for retro-reflective marking plates; the normal frequency of these verifications shall be once every two years.
Administrative provisions: penalties for non-conformity of production shall apply as set out in paragraph 3.6 of UN R150 (sub-paragraphs 3.6.1 and 3.6.2).
The approval granted may be withdrawn if the requirements of UN R150 are not met.

If a Contracting Party to the 1958 Agreement applying UN R150 withdraws a previously granted approval, it shall forthwith notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.

If the approval holder completely ceases to manufacture a retro-reflective device approved under UN R150, he shall inform the approving authority; upon receiving the communication, that authority shall inform the other Contracting Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation by means of a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1.

Administrative (UN R150 para 3.8): Contracting Parties applying this Regulation shall communicate to the United Nations secretariat the names and addresses of the Technical Services responsible for conducting approval tests and of the Type Approval Authorities which grant approval, and to which forms certifying approval, extension, refusal or withdrawal of approval, or definitive discontinuation of production issued in other countries, are to be sent.

The retro-reflecting device (rear retro-reflector) shall comply with the requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' and the Annexes referenced therein of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for type approval; the requirements pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the vehicle category/ies on which it is intended to be installed shall be applied where verification at the time of type approval is feasible.

For the purpose of this Regulation, retro-reflectors, retro-reflective marking materials, marking plates and advance warning triangles are referred to generally as 'retro-reflective devices'; the rear retro-reflector of the lamp shall be treated as a retro-reflective device under the requirements of para 4.

Retro-reflective devices shall be constructed so that they function satisfactorily and continue to do so in normal use, and shall not have any defect in design or manufacture detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The components of retro-reflective devices, or parts thereof, shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
Where retro-reflective marking materials are used, their means of attachment shall be durable and stable.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean; the surface shall not be rough and any protuberances shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
For retro-reflectors (a retro-reflective device under UN R150 para 4.1), the specific requirements of para 4.1.6 apply, namely those in paras 4.1.6.1 and 4.1.6.2.
A retro-reflector may consist of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, which shall be designed so that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
The colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters by means of paint or varnish is not permitted.

Colorimetric test conditions: the retro-reflecting device shall meet the requirements of sections 5 (General specifications) and 6 (Individual specifications) and the referenced Annexes of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, in the series of amendments in force at the time of application for type approval, pertinent to each retro-reflecting device and to the vehicle category on which it is installed.
Night-time colour of the retro-reflective device shall be verified using the test procedure for night time colours specified in para 4.2.1 (paras 4.2.1.1 to 4.2.1.3).
The night-time colour test specifications of para 4.2.1 apply only to white, red or amber retro-reflective devices.

When testing the colour of the retro-reflective device, illuminate it with CIE Standard Illuminant A, with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, with an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1; the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the retro-reflected light defined in UN Regulation No. 48.

White retro-reflective devices shall not produce a selective reflection: the trichromatic coordinates x and y of Standard Illuminant A used to illuminate the device shall not change by more than 0.01 after reflection by the device.

For testing the daytime colour of the retro-reflecting device material (UN R150 para 4.2.2, colorimetric test conditions), the material shall be illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using geometry (45a:0) or (0:45a) as described in Part 2 of Annex 4.

For the determination of the luminance factor of the retro-reflecting device, the sample shall be tested with the method described in Part 2 of Annex 4; the general requirements of sections 5 and 6 and referenced Annexes of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86 (series in force at application) also apply to this Regulation as pertinent to the device and vehicle category.
The retro-reflector of the rear lamp shall comply with the specific technical requirements set out in section 5 of UN R150.
The rear retro-reflector shall meet the technical requirements of paragraph 5.1 concerning retro-reflectors of Classes IA and IB (symbols IA and IB).

Every Class IA or IB retro-reflector, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7, shall meet: (a) the dimensions and shape requirements of Annex 5; (b) the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4 to 5.1.5; and (c) the physical and mechanical requirements of paragraph 5.1.7, depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.
The applicant shall submit ten samples of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector for approval, which shall be tested in the chronological order indicated in paragraph 5.1.7.
The retro-reflector shall be tested according to the test procedure of paragraph 5.1.3 (Class IA and IB retro-reflectors).

After verification of general specifications (para 4) and shape and dimensions (Annex 5), the ten samples shall undergo the heat resistance test (Annex 6 Part 1) and, at least one hour later, be examined for colorimetric characteristics (5.1.5) and RI (5.1.4) at 20' divergence and β1=β2=0° or, if necessary, in positions per Annex 4 Part 1 paras 1.1 and 1.2; the two samples with minimum and maximum values shall be fully tested per 5.1.4 and kept by the laboratory for further checks. The remaining eight samples are divided into four groups of two: first group water penetration test (Annex 6 Part 2) and, if satisfactory, fuel and lubricant resistance tests (Annex 7 Parts 1 and 2); second group, if necessary, corrosion test (Annex 6 Part 4) then abrasive-strength test of the rear face (Annex 6 Part 5); third group stability in time of optical properties (Annex 4 Part 3); fourth group resistance to weathering test (Annex 6 Part 6).

After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1 (test procedure for Class IA and IB retro-reflectors), the retro-reflectors in each group shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.1.3.2.1 and 5.1.3.2.2.
After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.5.

After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1, the retro-reflectors in each group shall have an RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4; the verification shall be performed only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
Class IA and IB retro-reflectors shall meet the minimum values of the coefficient of luminous intensity RI of retro-reflection as specified in paragraph 5.1.4 and its sub-paragraphs.

When applying for approval, the applicant shall specify one or more axes of reference, or a range of axes of reference, corresponding to the illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the table of coefficients of luminous intensity RI.

Where the manufacturer specifies more than one axis of reference or a range of different axes of reference, the photometric measurements shall be repeated, each time referring to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified by the manufacturer.

For photometric measurements of the retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system of the retro-reflective device, as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter for Class IA or IB, shall be considered; the illuminating surface shall be limited to 100 cm2, though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not attain this area; the manufacturer shall specify the perimeter of the area to be used.
The Class IA and Class IB retro-reflector shall meet the minimum RI values of retro-reflection specified for Class IA and Class IB under paragraph 5.1.4.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of red Class IA/IB retro-reflectors shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.

Retro-reflectors shall meet the minimum RI values (mcd/lx) of Table 3 for their class (IA/IB, IIIA/IIIB, IV), colour (white, amber, red), angles of divergence (20' and 1°30') and illumination angles (vertical β1 0°, ±10°, ±5°; horizontal β2 0°, ±20°, ±30°, ±40°, ±50°); for red IA/IB: 20' 300/200/100 and 1°30' 5/2.8/2.5 at the first three illumination angles; RI values lower than those in the last two columns of Table 3 are not permissible within the solid angle with the centre of reference as apex, bounded by planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).

Where a Class IA or IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
Class IA and IB retro-reflectors shall comply with the requirements concerning the colour of the reflected light of the device, as specified in paragraphs 5.1.5.1 and 5.1.5.2.
The colour (night-time colour) of the retro-reflector shall be tested according to the method described in paragraph 4.2.1.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

Retro-reflectors shall meet the special specification tests for resistance to external agents; depending on the materials of the retro-reflectors and their optical units, the Type Approval Authorities may authorize laboratories to omit certain unnecessary tests (only tests in Part 3 of Annex 4 and Parts 4, 5 and 6 of Annex 6), provided the omission is mentioned under 'Remarks' on the approval notification form.
The tests on Class IA and IB retro-reflectors shall be carried out in the chronological order of tests prescribed for them.

Retro-reflecting devices (Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB) shall be tested per the chronological order of tests in Table 4 across samples a to j, beginning with a visual inspection for general specifications on all ten samples.

Per Table 4 (Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB), all samples shall undergo visual inspection of shapes and dimensions (Annex 5), heat test 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C (Part 1 of Annex 6) with visual inspection for distortion, colorimetry (para 4.2; trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt) and limited photometry at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° (Part 1 of Annex 4); complete photometry on the designated samples; designated samples shall undergo water test (Part 3 of Annex 6) 10 min in normal and 10 min in inverted position, motor fuels 5 min (Part 1 of Annex 7), oils 5 min (Part 2 of Annex 7), corrosion 24 h, 2 h interval, 24 h, and rear face test 1 min (Part 4 of Annex 6), each followed by visual inspection, colorimetry and limited photometry as specified; stability in time (Part 3 of Annex 4) and resistance to weathering (Part 6 of Annex 6) shall be followed by colorimetry (visual or trichromatic) and limited photometry.

Retro-reflecting devices of Class IVA shall be tested per the chronological order in Table 5 across samples a to j: general and shape/dimension visual inspection on all samples; heat 48 h at 65 °C ± 2 °C with distortion inspection, colorimetry and limited photometry (20', β1 = β2 = 0°) on all samples; complete photometry on designated samples; water test (Part 2 of Annex 6) 10 min normal and 10 min inverted; motor fuels 5 min; oils 5 min; corrosion 24 h, 2 h interval, 24 h; rear face 1 min (Part 4 of Annex 6); impact (Part 4 of Annex 8); each followed by visual inspection, colorimetry (trichromatic coordinates in case of doubt) and limited photometry as specified.

The approval communication shall include a concise description stating whether the device is in isolation or part of an assembly of devices, the colour of light emitted (white/red/amber), whether installed as an integral part of a lamp integrated into the vehicle body (yes/no), geometric installation conditions and any variations, and whether only for limited mounting height of 750 mm or less above the ground (yes/no); inapplicable entries shall be struck out.
The approval communication shall state the position of the approval mark or Unique Identifier (UI).
The approval communication shall state whether approval is granted, refused, extended or withdrawn, striking out what does not apply.
The approval communication shall state the reason(s) for the extension, if applicable.
The approval communication shall state the place of issue.
The communication/approval form for the retro-reflective device (UN R150 Annex 5) shall state the date of issue (item 14: Date).
The approval communication form shall be signed and shall give the name of the signatory (item 15: Signature and Name).

The approval communication shall annex a list of the documents making up the approval file, deposited with the Type Approval Authority that granted approval, of which a copy can be obtained on request; the conformity of production control procedures (Annex 2 minimum requirements, General) apply to the approval.

Conformity of production requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if differences between production devices and the approved type do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.

With respect to photometric performance, conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices (e.g. the rear retro-reflector) shall not be contested if, when testing any retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.

The chromaticity coordinates shall be complied with in production; for each type of retro-reflective device the approval mark holder shall carry out at least the minimum verification tests at appropriate intervals, in accordance with this Regulation; if any sampling shows non-conformity for the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested; the manufacturer shall take steps to ensure conformity of the production concerned.
The manufacturer's conformity tests shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water, in accordance with this Regulation.
The methods used in the manufacturer's conformity tests shall be those specified in this Regulation for the corresponding tests of the retro-reflective device type.
Tests on the retro-reflective device (rear retro-reflector) shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in UN R150 (Annex 5, para 2.2.1).

In any conformity test carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent test methods may be used only with the consent of the Type Approval Authority; the manufacturer is responsible for proving that the applied methods are equivalent to those laid down in UN R150 (Annex 5, para 2.2.2).

Application of the test methods of paras 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 requires regular calibration of the test apparatus and its correlation with measurements made by a Type Approval Authority (Annex 5, para 2.2.3).
In all cases the reference methods shall be those of UN R150, particularly for the purpose of administrative verification and sampling (Annex 5, para 2.2.4).

Samples of retro-reflective devices shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch, i.e. a set of retro-reflective devices of the same type defined by the manufacturer's production methods; the assessment shall in general cover series production from individual factories, but a manufacturer may group records for the same type from several factories provided they operate under the same quality system and quality management (Annex 5, para 2.3, nature of sampling).

When the RI of a retro-reflective device is measured at illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0°, it shall be ascertained by slightly turning the device whether any mirror effect is produced; if there is such an effect, a reading shall be taken at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0° (Annex 5 Part 1, para 1.1).

At illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5 of the Regulation) and divergence angle 20', retro-reflective devices not marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their reference axes to the position of minimum RI, which shall conform to the value specified in paragraph 5; RI measurements at other illumination and divergence angles shall be made with the device in the position corresponding to this value of ε; if specified values are not attained, the device may be rotated about its reference axis ±5° from that position (Annex 5 Part 1, para 1.2).

At illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 4 of the Regulation) and divergence angle 20', retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall be rotated about their axes ±5°; the RI shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during this rotation (Annex 5 Part 1, para 1.3).

In the retro-reflector photometric test procedure (Annex 5 Part 1, para 1), if for the direction β1 = β2 = 0° and for ε = 0° the RI exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence shall be made for ε = 0°.

The retro-reflector photometric testing shall apply the definitions of Annex 5 Part 1 para 2 (basic definitions in para 2.3 of the Regulation; Figures A4-I to A4-III): reference centre C; illumination axis I; observation axis O; observation angle α (divergence angle); entrance angle β1/β2 (vertical component given first; full range -90° < β1 < 90° and -180° < β2 < 180°; also called illumination angle); angle of rotation ε (origin at the 'TOP' datum mark if marked); angular aperture of the measuring device γ; of the source δ; of the retro-reflecting device η.
The photometry of retro-reflective devices shall comply with the dimensional and physical specifications given in Annex 5 Part 1 para 3 (heading for paras 3.1 to 3.4).
The CIE angular system as shown in Figure A4-I shall be used for specifying and measuring retro-reflective devices and marking materials.

The CIE co-ordinate system of Figure A4-I shall be realised with a suitable support (goniometer) such as in Figure A4-II, embodying the CIE angular system, with all axes, angles and directions of rotation positive; the principal axis is the illumination axis; the first axis is fixed perpendicular to the plane containing the observation and illumination axes; the second axis is perpendicular to both the first axis and the reference axis; the reference axis is fixed in the retro-reflective device and moved with β1 and β2, its rotation being given by ε.
The goniometer mechanism embodying the CIE angular system shall be as in Figure A4-II, or any equivalent arrangement of the components.
For testing retro-reflection, the retro-reflective devices shall be illuminated with CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) and measured as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.

The measuring geometry shall be as described in Figure A4-III with the limits: angular diameter of the source δ ≤ 10'; angular diameter of the measuring device γ ≤ 10'; angular diameter of the illuminated area η ≤ 80'.

The photometric measurement of the retro-reflector (retro-reflective device) of the rear lamp shall be carried out using the measuring geometry illustrated in Figure A4-III of UN R150 Annex 4 (angles δ, γ and η and the measuring distance).
During photometric measurements of the rear lamp's retro-reflective device, stray reflections should be avoided by appropriate masking.

For the photometry of the retro-reflective device, the measuring distance shall be chosen so that at least the limits for the angles δ, γ and η given in Annex 5 Part 1 para 3 and illustrated in Figure A4-III are respected, and the distance shall not be less than 10 m.

For the photometry of the retro-reflective device, the illuminance over its useful area, measured perpendicular to the incident light, shall be sufficiently uniform; this shall be checked with a measuring element whose sensitive area is not greater than one-tenth of the area examined, and the variation of illuminance shall satisfy max/min ≤ 1.05.
The photometer head (measuring element) used for the photometry of the retro-reflective device shall comply with the requirements of Annex 5 Part 1 para 3.8 (subparagraphs 3.8.1 and 3.8.2).
The photometer head used for the photometry of the retro-reflective device shall be corrected to the spectral luminous efficiency of the CIE standard photometric observer in photopic vision.

The photometer head shall not show a perceptible change in local sensitivity within the area of its aperture; otherwise suitable provisions shall be added, e.g. application of a diffusing window at a certain distance in front of the sensitive surface.

Measurement precautions in the photometry of retro-reflection shall be observed for the retro-reflector: best practice procedures described in the relevant CIE reports and standards shall be considered, together with the items outlined in Annex 5 Part 1 para 4.

In the photometry of retro-reflection (Annex 5 Part 1, para 4 measurement precautions, with best practice per the relevant CIE reports and standards), the precautions on residual and stray light given in para 4.1 shall be considered when measuring the rear retro-reflector.

Because very low light levels are measured, precautions shall minimise stray light errors: the background to the sample and the sample holder framework should be matt black, and the field of view of the photometer head and the spread of light from both the sample and the source shall be restricted as much as possible.
Reflections from the floor and walls occurring over the relatively long test distances shall be screened from both the sample and the photometer head by baffles.

Residual stray light shall always be corrected for by measuring it with the sample covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape, or a specular black surface suitably oriented with a light trap; this value shall be subtracted from the value measured on the retro-reflective device.
In the photometry of retro-reflection, the apparatus stability precautions of para 4.2 shall be considered (best practice per the relevant CIE reports and standards).

The light source and photometer head should remain stable throughout the test period; as photometer head sensitivity and V(λ) adaptation change with temperature, laboratory ambient temperature should not vary significantly during testing; sufficient time should be allowed for the apparatus to stabilise before measurements begin.
To check the overall stability of the reflex photometer during a series of tests, periodic measurements of RI values of a stable reference standard should be made.

The goniometer used for retro-reflection measurements in the CIE geometry shall be as defined in paragraph 2.3 of the Regulation and illustrated in Figure A4-II (photometer head O arbitrarily shown vertically above source I; first axis fixed, horizontal and perpendicular to the observation half-plane); any equivalent arrangement of the components may be used.

For testing the daytime colour and luminance factor of retro-reflective material, illumination by CIE Standard Illuminant D65 (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006) using measurement geometry 45a:0 shall be used.

Daytime colour of retro-reflective material shall be measured with a spectrophotometer per CIE 15:2004, illuminated polychromatically or by monochromator (stepwise resolution not larger than 10 nm) with CIE D65 at 45° to the normal and viewed along the normal (geometry 45/0); alternatively simulated D65 spectra are allowed if the same accuracy is verified, with simulation quality assessed per ISO 23603:2005(E)/CIE S 012/E:2004 and spectral distribution of category BC (CIELAB) or better; measurement area at least 4.0 cm²; per CIE 15 the aperture is irradiated uniformly from all directions between cones of 40° and 50° half angle and the receiver collects all radiation within a 5° half angle cone about the normal; the annular geometry may be approximated by a ring of light sources or fibre bundles, or by a single source with sample rotation giving equal weight to all circumferential angles; apertures of source and receiver shall be sufficiently large relative to distances; notes on flares/sparkles of micro-prismatic materials, approximation of the annular principle and measurement uncertainty apply.
The approval granting authority has the right to test the stability of optical properties of a retro-reflecting material in use (when used for marking or as distinctive markings/graphics).

Type Approval Authorities of Contracting Parties in which approval was granted may undertake the same tests; if systematic failures in use occur for a type of retro-reflective material, the tested material samples shall be transferred for appraisal to the authority which granted approval.
If other criteria are missing, the notation of systematic failures in use for a type of retro-reflective material shall be established according to paragraph 5 in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The authority which granted approval shall have the right to check the stability in time of the optical properties of a type of rear marking plate in service.

Type Approval Authorities of countries other than the approving country may carry out similar checks in their territory; if a type of rear marking plate in use exhibits a systematic defect, they shall transmit any components removed for examination to the approving authority, with a request for its opinion.

In the absence of other criteria, the concept of systematic defect of a type of rear marking plate in use shall be interpreted in conformity with paragraph 5 of Part 3 of Annex 4; the following Annex 5 heading covers specifications of shape and dimensions of retro-reflective devices of Class IA or IB.

The approval granting authority may test the optical properties stability of a retro-reflecting material in use (when used for marking or as distinctive markings/graphics); the shape of the illuminating surfaces shall not be easily confused, from an observation distance of 10 metres, with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors in paragraph 2.1 (Classes IIIA and IIIB).

The Type Approval Authorities of Contracting Parties that granted approval may undertake the same tests, and if systematic failures in use occur for a type of retro-reflective material, the tested samples shall be transferred to the approving authority for appraisal; the illuminating surfaces of retro-reflective devices of Classes IIIA and IIIB shall have the shape of an equilateral triangle, and if the word "TOP" is inscribed in one corner, the apex of that corner shall be directed upwards.

The illuminating surface of Class IIIA and IIIB retro-reflective devices may or may not have at its centre a triangular, non-retro-reflecting area, with sides parallel to those of the outer triangle (subject to the Type Approval Authorities' right to test and to transfer samples in case of systematic failures in use).
The illuminating surface may or may not be continuous; in any case the shortest distance between two adjacent retro-reflecting optical units shall not exceed 15 mm.

The illuminating surface of a retro-reflective device shall be considered continuous if the edges of the illuminating surfaces of adjacent separate optical units are parallel and the optical units are evenly distributed over the whole solid surface of the triangle.
If the illuminated surface is not continuous, the number of separate retro-reflecting optical units, including the corner units, shall be not less than four on each side of the triangle.
Where the illuminated surface is not continuous, the separate retro-reflecting optical units shall not be replaceable unless they consist of approved retro-reflective devices of Class IA.

The outside edges of the illuminating surfaces of triangular retro-reflective devices of Classes IIIA and IIIB shall be between 150 and 200 mm long; for hollow-triangle type devices, the width of the sides, measured at right angles to them, shall be at least 20 per cent of the effective length between the extremities of the illuminating surface.

Where other criteria are missing, the notation "systematic failures in use" for a type of retro-reflective material is established per paragraph 5 in Part 3 of Annex 4; the shape of the light emitting surfaces shall not be easily confused, from an observation distance of 10 metres, with the triangular shape prescribed for retro-reflectors in paragraph 2.1.

Shape and dimensions of the triangle: the retro-reflecting strip may be continuous or not; if not continuous, the free area of the supporting material shall be red (see also paragraph 5.9.4.2.1. of this Regulation).

Shape and dimensions of the triangle: for an advance warning triangle of type 1, the fluorescent surface shall be continuous to the retro-reflecting units and arranged symmetrically along the three sides of the triangle; in use its surface area shall be not less than 315 cm2; an edging, continuous or not, not more than 5 mm wide, not necessarily red, may be placed between the retro-reflecting surface and the fluorescent surface.
Shape and dimensions of the triangle: the side of the open centre of the triangle shall have a minimum length of 70 mm (Figure A5-VIII).
The shape and dimensions of the support of the advance warning triangle shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 8.2 of Annex 5 Part 3 (heading for the support provisions).
Shape and dimensions of the support: the distance between the supporting surface and the lower side of the advance warning triangle shall not exceed 300 mm.
The fluorescent retro-reflecting material shall be coloured in the mass, either in the retro-reflective elements or as a solid surface layer.
Environmental testing shall be carried out in accordance with Annex 6 of UN R150 (heading of the Annex covering environmental test requirements).
The retro-reflective device shall be subjected to and satisfy the Annex 6 Part 1 resistance to heat test (Part 1 - Resistance to heat) as described in the following clauses.

For moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflective device shall be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, after which the sample shall be allowed to cool for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.

Where flexible materials are used for Classes C, D, E, F, Marking plates of Classes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and advance warning triangle of type 2, a section of a sample unit not less than 300 mm long shall be kept for 12 hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 °C ± 2 °C, then cooled for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C, then kept for 12 hours at -20 °C ± 2 °C, and examined after a recovery time of 4 hours under normal laboratory conditions.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, in particular of its optical component, shall be visible.
Retro-reflective devices shall be subjected to and satisfy the Annex 6 Part 2 test for resistance to water penetration as described in the following clauses.
Retro-reflectors and retro-reflective marking materials shall be tested for resistance to water penetration according to the procedure of paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2 of Annex 6 Part 2.

Retro-reflective devices, whether part of a lamp or not, or a sample unit of retro-reflective marking, shall be stripped of all removable parts and immersed for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the water surface; the test shall be repeated after turning the device through 180° so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water; the sample units shall then be immediately immersed under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.

No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit; if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device shall not be considered to have passed the test.

If visual inspection after the water-immersion test of retro-reflectors and retro-reflective marking materials (UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2, paragraph 1) does not reveal the presence of water, or in case of doubt, the further measurements specified in paragraphs 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 shall be carried out.

In the case of retro-reflectors, where visual inspection does not reveal water or in case of doubt, the RI shall be measured by the method described in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2 of UN R150, the retro-reflective device being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.

In the case of a sample unit of retro-reflective marking, where visual inspection does not reveal water or in case of doubt, the coefficient of retro-reflection R' shall be measured in conformity with Part 2 of Annex 6, the sample unit being first lightly shaken to remove excess water from the outside.
Advance warning triangles shall be tested in accordance with the test requirements of UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2, paragraph 2 (heading clause covering the tests for advance warning triangles).
The retro-reflective device or fluorescent retro-reflecting material of advance warning triangles shall be subjected to the resistance test specified in UN R150 Annex 6 Part 2, paragraph 2.1.

For the resistance test, the triangle (collapsible triangles assembled as for use) shall be immersed for 10 minutes in water at 50 °C ± 5 °C, with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface about 20 mm below the water surface; immediately afterwards the retro-reflective device shall be immersed under the same conditions in water at 25 °C ± 5 °C.

After the immersion test, no water shall have penetrated to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflective device; if visual inspection clearly reveals the presence of water, the device has failed; water or water vapour penetration into the edges of fluorescent retro-reflecting materials shall not be deemed a failure.

If visual inspection does not reveal water, or in case of doubt, the RI shall be measured again under the same conditions as specified in paragraph 1.2 of Part 2 of Annex 6, after the retro-reflective device has been gently shaken to remove excess water from the outside; the RI shall not have diminished by more than 40 per cent of the values recorded before the test.

Water test for advance warning triangles: the triangle (collapsible triangles assembled as for use) shall be immersed flat for two hours at the bottom of a water tank at 25 °C ± 5 °C, with the active face upwards and 5 cm under the water surface; it shall then be removed and dried; no part of the device may show clear signs of deterioration which might impair the effectiveness of the triangle.
Retro-reflective marking plates shall be subjected to the tests specified in Annex 6 Part 2 paragraph 3 (heading for the test for retro-reflective marking plates).

Resistance to water for retro-reflective marking plates: a section of a sample unit not less than 300 mm long shall be immersed in distilled water at 23 ± 5 °C for 18 hours, then left to dry for 24 hours under normal laboratory conditions; after the test the section shall be examined and no part inside 10 mm from the cut edge shall show evidence of deterioration which would reduce the effectiveness of the plate.

Part 3 provides alternative test procedures for resistance to water penetration of retro-reflective devices of Classes IB and IIIB; where applied, these alternative procedures shall be used in place of the standard water resistance test.
As an alternative, at the request of the manufacturer, the moisture test and dust test of Annex 6 Part 3 shall be applied.

The moisture test shall evaluate the ability of the sample device to resist moisture penetration from a water spray and shall determine the drainage capability of devices with drain holes or other exposed openings.
The water spray test for the moisture test shall be performed using a water spray cabinet having the characteristics specified in the following paragraphs.

The water spray cabinet shall be equipped with nozzle(s) providing a solid cone water spray of sufficient angle to completely cover the sample device; the centreline of the nozzle(s) shall be directed downward at an angle of 45° ± 5° to the vertical axis of a rotating test platform.

For the water spray test equipment (water spray cabinet) used in the moisture test, the rotating test platform shall have a minimum diameter of 140 mm and shall rotate about a vertical axis in the centre of the cabinet.

For the water spray test equipment, the precipitation rate of the water spray at the device shall be 2.5 (+1.6/-0) mm/min, measured with a vertical cylindrical collector centred on the vertical axis of the rotating test platform; the collector height shall be 100 mm and its inside diameter shall be a minimum of 140 mm.

In the moisture test, which evaluates the ability of the sample device to resist moisture penetration from a water spray and determines drainage capability of devices with drain holes or other exposed openings, a sample device mounted on a test fixture, with initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to the water spray test procedure specified in the following sub-clauses.
During the water spray test, all drain holes and other openings of the sample device shall remain open; drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.
During the water spray test, the device shall be rotated about its vertical axis at a rate of 4.0 ± 0.5 min-1.

If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated during the water spray test at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate) and 55 min OFF.
The water spray test shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).
After the water spray test, the rotation and the water spray shall be turned OFF and the device shall be allowed to drain for 1 hour with the cabinet door closed.

Water spray test sample evaluation (UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3, para 2.2.6): upon completion of the drain period, observe the interior of the device for moisture accumulation; no standing pool of water shall be present or be formable by tapping or tilting the device; after drying the exterior with a dry cotton cloth, measure the RI according to the method in Part 1 of Annex 4.

Dust exposure test (UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3, para 2.3): the sample device shall be subjected to a dust exposure test that evaluates its ability to resist dust penetration which could significantly affect the photometric output of the retro-reflector.
Dust exposure test equipment (UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3, para 2.3.1): the equipment specified in the following paragraphs (test chamber and test dust) shall be used to test for dust exposure.

Dust exposure test chamber (UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3, para 2.3.2): the chamber interior shall be cubical, 0.9 to 1.5 m per side, optionally with a hopper-shaped bottom to collect dust; internal volume excluding the hopper bottom shall be at most 2 m3 and charged with 3 to 5 kg of test dust; the chamber shall be able to agitate the dust with compressed air or blower fans so that the dust is diffused throughout the chamber.
Test dust (UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3, para 2.3.3): the test dust used shall be fine powdered cement in accordance with ASTM C 150-84 (American Society for Testing and Materials).

Dust exposure test procedure (UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3, para 2.3.4): a sample device mounted on a test fixture, with the initial RI measured and recorded, shall be exposed to dust as specified in the following paragraphs.
Device openings during dust exposure test (UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3, para 2.3.5): all drain holes and other openings shall remain open; drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the device.

Dust exposure (UN R150 Annex 6 Part 3, para 2.3.6): place the mounted device in the dust chamber no closer than 150 mm from a wall; devices longer than 600 mm shall be horizontally centred in the chamber; agitate the test dust as completely as possible with compressed air or blower(s) at 15 min intervals for 2 to 15 s each, for a duration of 5 hours; allow the dust to settle between agitation periods.

Upon completion of the dust exposure test of the retro-reflector sample, the exterior of the device shall be cleaned and dried with a dry cotton cloth and the coefficient of retro-reflection RI shall be measured according to the method specified in paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of UN R150.
The retro-reflective device shall be subjected to and comply with the resistance to corrosion test requirements specified in Part 4 of Annex 6 of UN R150.

Retro-reflective devices shall be designed to retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed; the resistance of the front surface to tarnishing and of the protection of the rear face to deterioration shall be checked, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked; corrosion resistance testing is described in ISO 9227:2017.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, shall be stripped of all removable parts and subjected to saline mist for 50 hours, comprising two exposure periods of 24 hours each, separated by a two-hour interval during which the sample is allowed to dry.

For retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the saline mist shall be produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution of 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride dissolved in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent impurities.
The retro-reflective device shall meet the requirements specified after the corrosion test (paragraphs 4.1 and 4.2 of Annex 6 Part 4).
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

After the corrosion test, the surface shall be cleaned to remove salt deposits from the saline mist; when measured after a 48-hour recovery period as specified in Part 2 of Annex 6, at entrance angle β2 = 5° and observation angle α = 20', the coefficient of retro-reflection RA of the retro-reflective areas shall be not less than the value in Table 9 and not more than the value in Table 10.

The accessible rear face of mirror-backed retro-reflective devices (the rear retro-reflector of the lamp) shall be verified for resistance in accordance with the test procedure of Part 5 of Annex 6 of UN R150.

For moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and Advance warning triangle of type 1, the resistance of the accessible rear face of mirror-backed retro-reflective devices shall be tested as specified in Part 5 of Annex 6.
During the test, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be brushed with a hard nylon brush.

After brushing, for moulded plastics reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB and IVA, a cotton cloth soaked in the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7 shall be applied to the rear face of the retro-reflective device for one minute; the cloth shall then be removed and the device left to dry.

After brushing, for moulded plastics reflectors of Advance warning triangle of type 1, the reverse side of the retro-reflective device shall be covered or thoroughly wetted for one minute with the mixture defined in Part 1 of Annex 7; the fuel shall then be removed and the device allowed to dry.
As soon as evaporation is completed, the reverse side shall be brushed again with the same brush as used before.
The RI (coefficient of retro-reflection) shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of UN R150 after the whole surface of the mirror-backed rear face has been covered with Indian ink.

For the retro-reflector of an Advance warning triangle of type 1, the RI shall not have diminished by more than 40 per cent of the values recorded before the test; this test is not applicable for fluorescent retro-reflecting material.
The retro-reflective rear lamp components (e.g. the retro-reflector and its lens) shall be tested for resistance to weathering in accordance with Part 6 of Annex 6 of UN R150.
The resistance to weathering test of the retro-reflective device shall be performed as accelerated artificial weathering, as specified in Part 6 of Annex 6 of UN R150.

For accelerated artificial weathering, the test apparatus shall be in accordance with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013, shall be capable of controlling temperature and relative humidity, and shall be equipped with a water spray system.
The water spray system of the weathering apparatus shall be capable of spraying a minimum of 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
The spray water used in the weathering apparatus shall comply with the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
For temperature measurement during accelerated artificial weathering, either a Black-Standard or a Black-Panel thermometer may be used (test methods TM1 and TM2).
The test method used for the weathering test (TM1 or TM2) shall be specified in the test report.

The samples shall be exposed in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the parameters given in Table A6-1, for a period of 500 hours in the case of retro-reflective devices (such as the rear retro-reflector), or for 100 hours in the case of fluorescent materials.

Accelerated artificial weathering test (Table A6-1) shall use one of two parameter sets. TM1, black-standard thermometer, cycle No. 1 per EN ISO 4892-2:2013: 102 min dry then 18 min water spray; irradiance 60 ± 2 W/m² broadband (300 to 400 nm) and 0.51 ± 0.02 W/m² narrowband (340 nm); black-standard temperature 65 ± 3 °C; relative humidity 50 ± 10 %. TM2, black-panel thermometer, cycle No. 4: 102 min dry then 18 min water spray; same irradiance values; black-panel temperature 63 ± 3 °C; relative humidity 50 ± 10 %. The two thermometers display different temperatures and results need not be identical; the sensor best correlating with the samples is recommended (e.g. black-panel for reflective material on aluminium substrate). Specimen preparation shall follow EN ISO 4892-2:2013; relocating samples in the xenon tester regularly (e.g. 4-8 times per test) is good lab practice. In case of dispute natural outdoor exposure results prevail. The ± tolerances are allowable fluctuations about the set value under equilibrium conditions, not permitted variation of the value.
The rear lamp, including its retro-reflector and lens, shall be subjected to the chemical testing specified in Annex 7 of UN R150.
The resistance to fuels shall be verified in accordance with Part 1 of Annex 7 (Resistance to fuels) of UN R150.

A test mixture of 70 vol. per cent n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent toluol shall be used for the fuel resistance test of either a retro-reflective device or a sample unit of retro-reflective marking material, as specified in paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.

For a retro-reflective device (such as the rear retro-reflector), the outer surface, in particular the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture (70 vol. % n-heptane, 30 vol. % toluol); after about five minutes the surface shall be visually inspected and shall show no apparent surface changes, except that slight surface cracks are not objected to.

For a sample unit of retro-reflective marking material, a section not less than 300 mm long shall be immersed in the test mixture (70 vol. % n-heptane, 30 vol. % toluol) for one minute; after removal, the surface shall be wiped dry with a soft cloth and shall show no visible change that would reduce its effective performance.
Advance warning triangles shall be tested for resistance to fuels as specified in paragraph 2.1 of Annex 7 Part 1.

For advance warning triangles, the triangle and its protective cover shall be immersed separately in a tank containing 70 per cent n-heptane and 30 per cent toluene; after 60 seconds they shall be removed and drained of excess liquid; the triangle shall then be placed in its cover and the unit laid flat in a still atmosphere; when completely dried, the triangle shall not adhere to its cover and shall show no visually noticeable change on its surface or apparent detrimental modifications, although slight surface cracks may be tolerated.
Annex 7 Part 2 (Resistance to lubricating oils): the rear retro-reflector of the lamp shall be subjected to and withstand the resistance to lubricating oils test as defined in this part.

For moulded plastics retro-reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangle of type 1 (including the rear retro-reflector of the lamp, if of these classes), the test procedure for resistance to lubricating oils of Annex 7 Part 2 shall be applied.

For moulded plastics retro-reflectors of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangle of type 1: the outer surface of the retro-reflective device, in particular the illuminating surface, shall be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil; after about 5 minutes the surface shall be cleaned; the RI shall then be measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. of this Regulation.
Annex 8 Mechanical Testing: the retro-reflective device of the lamp shall meet the mechanical testing requirements specified in Annex 8.
Annex 8 Part 1: resistance to cleaning shall be demonstrated in the case of a sample unit of retro-reflective marking materials, according to the manual cleaning and power washing tests of this part.

Manual cleaning: a test sample smeared with a mixture of detergent lubricating oil and graphite shall be easily cleaned without damage to the retro-reflective surface when wiped with a mild aliphatic solvent such as n-heptane, followed by washing with a neutral detergent.

Power washing: when subjected to continuous spraying for 60 seconds on the test component in its normal mounting conditions, a test sample shall show no damage to the retro-reflective surface, no delamination from the substrate and no separation from the sample mounting surface, with: (a) water/wash solution pressure 8 ± 0.2 MPa; (b) temperature 60 +0/-5 °C; (c) flow rate 7 ± 1 l/min; (d) cleaning wand tip positioned 600 ± 20 mm from the retro-reflective surface; (e) wand held at no greater angle than 45 degrees from perpendicular to the surface; (f) 40-degree nozzle creating a wide fan pattern.
Annex 8 Part 2: bonding strength shall be verified in the case of adhesive materials, where adhesive is used for the retro-reflective material of the lamp.
In case retro-reflective marking material is used, the bonding strength test shall use an aluminium plate as the substrate, with the material applied according to the manufacturer's recommendation.

In case retro-reflective marking material is used, its adhesion shall be determined after 24 hours curing time using a 90-degree peel on a tensile strength testing machine, on an aluminium plate substrate with application per the manufacturer's recommendation.
In case retro-reflective marking material is used, the material shall not be easily removable from the aluminium test substrate without damaging the material.

In case retro-reflective marking material is used, the material shall require a force of at least 10 N per 25 mm width, at a constant speed of 300 mm per minute, to be removed from its substrate (aluminium plate, application per the manufacturer's recommendation).
Retro-reflecting marking materials shall be subjected to the flexing test as specified in Part 3 of Annex 8.
For retro-reflective marking material samples intended to be adhered to a flexible substrate, e.g. tarpaulin, the flexing test requirements of Annex 8 Part 3 shall apply.

For samples to be adhered to a flexible substrate, e.g. tarpaulin, a specimen of the sample unit measuring 50 mm by 300 mm shall be bent once lengthwise around a 3.2 mm mandrel, with the adhesive contacting the mandrel for a period of 1 second.

For samples to be adhered to a flexible substrate, e.g. tarpaulin, the flexing test shall be conducted at a test temperature of 23 °C ± 2 °C; note: for ease of testing, talcum powder may be spread on the adhesive to prevent sticking to the mandrel.
After the test, the specimen shall not show cracking of the surface and shall not show any visible change that would reduce its effective performance.
Part 4 - Resistance to impact: the device shall be subjected to and comply with the impact resistance test requirements specified in this Part.

Rear marking plates (except plastics corner-cube reflectors): when a 25 mm diameter solid steel ball is dropped from a height of 2 m onto the retro-reflective and fluorescent surfaces of a supported plate at an ambient temperature of 23 ± 2 °C, the material shall show no cracking or separation from the substrate at a distance of more than 5 mm from the impacted area.

Retro-reflective devices of Class IVA: mount the device similarly to its mounting on the vehicle, with the lens horizontal and facing upwards; drop a 13 mm diameter polished solid steel ball once, vertically, onto the central part of the lens from a height of 0.76 m (ball may be guided but not restricted in free fall); when tested at room temperature the lens shall not crack.
General specifications: the lighting and light-signalling devices shall comply with the general specifications of paragraph 5 of UN R48 and its subparagraphs.

Lighting and light-signalling devices shall be fitted so that, under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply with it; in particular, it shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.
The illuminating lamps described in paragraphs 2.5.1., 2.5.2. and 2.5.10. shall be installed so that correct adjustment of their orientation can easily be carried out.

In the case of headlamps fitted with measures to prevent discomfort to other road-users in a country where traffic operates on the opposite side of the road to that for which the headlamp was designed, such measures shall be achieved automatically or by the vehicle user with the vehicle in park condition without special tools (other than those provided with the vehicle); detailed instructions shall be provided by the vehicle manufacturer with the vehicle; this does not apply to dedicated objects that may be added to the exterior of the headlamp.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road and, in addition, perpendicular to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle for side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, and parallel to that plane for all other signalling devices (including the rear lamp); a tolerance of ±3° shall be allowed in each direction; any specific fitting instructions laid down by the manufacturer shall also be complied with.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2., and, where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.5.1 to 5.5.5 (symmetrical fitting, symmetry of the lamps, same colorimetric requirements, substantially identical photometric characteristics, and logo restrictions).

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be fitted to the vehicle symmetrically in relation to the median longitudinal plane, the assessment being based on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp and not on the edge of its illuminating surface referred to in paragraph 2.10.3.

In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall be symmetrical to one another in relation to the median longitudinal plane; this requirement does not apply to the interior structure of the lamp.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics; this does not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.

In the absence of specific instructions, where lamps incorporate a manufacturer logo, only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo may be fitted on the rear of the vehicle, and only two lateral logos (one on each side) or one central logo on the front of the vehicle; all logos that are not vehicle manufacturer or body manufacturer logos are prohibited.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the general specifications of paragraph 5 (the requirements for lamp installation) shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps and single lamps shall comply with the provisions of paragraph 5.7 of UN R48 (heading for the rules on lamp grouping, combination and reciprocal incorporation).

Lamps (e.g. rear position, stop, reversing lamp and retro-reflector in one housing) may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another provided that all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any, are fulfilled.

The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which it is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF; however, when a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other functions that can be switched ON together with it, the colour requirements of each of those other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.
Stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps shall not be reciprocally incorporated with one another.
Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, the conditions of paragraphs 5.7.1.3.1 and 5.7.1.3.2 shall be met.

Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, any horizontal or vertical straight line passing through the projections of the apparent surfaces of these functions on a plane perpendicular to the reference axis shall not intersect more than two borderlines separating adjacent areas of different colour.

Where stop lamps and direction-indicator lamps are grouped, their apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, based upon the areas bounded by the outline of their light emitting surfaces, shall not overlap.
Single lamps within the scope of UN R48 para 5.7 (grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated or single lamps) shall comply with the installation requirements of paragraph 5.7.2 for single lamps.

Single lamps as defined in para 2.14.11.1 subparagraph (a) whose apparent surface consists of two or more distinct parts shall be installed so that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis, is not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the apparent surface in that direction; or (b) the minimum distance between facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, does not exceed 75 mm; these requirements do not apply to a single retro-reflector.

Single lamps as defined in para 2.4.11.1 subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro-reflectors, shall be installed so that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of those apparent surfaces; or (b) the minimum distance between facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or two independent retro-reflectors, measured perpendicularly to the reference axis, does not exceed 75 mm.

Single lamps as defined in para 2.4.11.1 subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1; two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces included in the same lamp body and/or having a common outer lens shall not be considered an interdependent lamp system; however, a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

Two lamps or an even number of lamps in the shape of a band or strip shall be placed symmetrically relative to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, extend on both sides to within at least 0.4 m of the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, and be not less than 0.8 m long; illumination of such a surface shall be provided by not less than two light sources placed as close as possible to the ends; the light-emitting surface may consist of juxtaposed elements provided the individual light-emitting surfaces, when projected on a transverse plane, fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

The maximum height above the ground shall be measured from the highest point and the minimum height from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis; where the maximum and minimum heights above the ground clearly meet the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.
For the purpose of reducing the geometric visibility angles, the position of a lamp with regard to height above the ground shall be measured from the H plane.

In the case of a dipped-beam headlamp, the minimum height above the ground shall be measured from the lowest point of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, independent of its utilization.

For the position of the lamp as regards width (UN R48 para 5.8, where maximum/minimum height is measured on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis), the position shall be determined from the edge of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis furthest from the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle when referred to overall width, and from the inner edges of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis when referred to the distance between lamps; where the position as regards width clearly meets the requirements of the Regulation, the exact edges of any surface need not be determined.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics of the rear lamp functions (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface) shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

Direction-indicator lamps, the vehicle-hazard warning signal, amber side-marker lamps complying with paragraph 6.18.7 of UN R48, and the emergency stop signal shall be flashing lamps; if the rear lamp incorporates a direction-indicator function (not listed for this product) it shall be a flashing lamp, while rear position, stop and reversing functions remain non-varied in operation per para 5.9.

The photometric characteristics of any lamp (including rear position, stop and reversing functions) may vary only (a) in relation to the ambient light, (b) as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or (c) when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, provided that any variation complies with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.

If a direction indicator lamp of categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a or 2b is used (not listed for this product), its photometric characteristics may be varied during a flash by sequential activation of light sources as specified in paragraph 5.6 of UN Regulation No. 6 or paragraph 5.6.11 of UN Regulation No. [LSD]; this provision shall not apply when direction indicator lamps of categories 2a and 2b are operated as emergency stop signal according to paragraph 6.23.1 of UN R48.

If an answer-back signal is provided using the lamp(s), the signal may flash and/or vary in luminous intensity and/or vary in apparent surface, and the lamp(s) used for the answer-back signal shall operate according to the conditions specified in the general specifications and/or in dedicated paragraph 6.27 of UN R48.
