If the reversing lamp provides a reversing projection, the projection may vary according to the steering wheel angle and/or the speed of the vehicle and/or the proximity to an obstacle.

The rear lamp shall comply with the provisions of UN R48 para 5.10 regarding light which could give rise to confusion (heading of the provisions listed under that paragraph); no light emitted by the lamp shall give rise to confusion.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in UN R48 paragraph 2.1.5) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.
White light emitted by a lamp fitted on the front of the vehicle (as defined in UN R48 paragraph 2.1.5) shall not be visible from the rear of the vehicle.

When assessing light that could give rise to confusion under paragraph 5.10, no account shall be taken of lighting devices fitted for the interior lighting of the vehicle nor of reversing projections.

Compliance with paragraphs 5.10.1 (red light from rear lamps not visible from the front) and 5.10.2 (white light from front lamps not visible from the rear) shall be verified according to the methods of paragraphs 5.10.4.1 to 5.10.4.3.

To verify paragraph 5.10.1, for visibility of red light towards the front of the vehicle, with the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp when viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

To verify paragraph 5.10.2, for visibility of white light towards the rear of the vehicle, with the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp when viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirements of paragraphs 5.10.4.1 and 5.10.4.2 shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the red light emitted to the front and/or the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps (if they exist), the side-marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.

The simultaneous ON/OFF switching of the front and rear position lamps, end-outline marker lamps (if present), side-marker lamps (if present) and rear registration plate lamp (para 5.11) need not apply while any of the following exists: (a) front and rear position lamps, and side-marker lamps combined or reciprocally incorporated with them, are switched ON as parking lamps; (b) side-marker lamps flash in conjunction with direction indicators; (c) daytime running lamps are switched ON; (d) the front position lamp function is substituted under paragraph 5.12.1.

In the case of an interdependent lamp system, all light sources shall be switched ON and OFF simultaneously, so that the front and rear position lamps, end-outline marker lamps (if present), side-marker lamps (if present) and rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF together.

The electrical connections shall be such that main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps cannot be switched ON unless the lamps referred to in paragraph 5.11 (front and rear position lamps, end-outline marker lamps if present, side-marker lamps if present, rear registration plate lamp) are also switched ON; this does not apply to main-beam or dipped-beam headlamps whose luminous warnings consist of intermittent lighting up at short intervals of the main-beam headlamp, or of the dipped-beam headlamp, or alternate lighting up at short intervals of the main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps.
Dipped-beam headlamps and/or main-beam headlamps and/or front fog lamps may substitute the function of the front position lamps only if the conditions of paragraphs 5.12.1.1 to 5.12.1.3 are met.

Where dipped-beam headlamps, main-beam headlamps and/or front fog lamps substitute the front position lamp function, their electrical connections shall be such that, in case of failure of any of these lighting devices, the front position lamps are automatically switched ON again.

Where dipped-beam headlamps, main-beam headlamps and/or front fog lamps substitute the front position lamp function, the substituting lamp/function shall meet, for the respective position lamp, the requirements concerning: (a) the geometric visibility prescribed for front position lamps in 6.9.5; and (b) the minimum photometric values according to the angles of light distribution.

Where a lamp substitutes the front position lamp function, appropriate evidence demonstrating compliance with the requirements of paragraph 5.12.1.2 (geometric visibility per 6.9.5 and minimum photometric values according to light distribution angles) shall be provided in the test reports of the substituting lamp.
Where a closed-circuit tell-tale is prescribed by this Regulation, it may be replaced by an "operating" tell-tale.
Concealable lamps (UN R48 para 5.14): the rear lamp shall comply with the provisions of para 5.14 on concealable lamps, as set out in paras 5.14.1 to 5.14.5.

Concealment of lamps is prohibited, except main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps, which may be concealed when not in use; the rear lamp functions (rear position, stop, reversing, retro-reflector) shall therefore not be concealable.

In the event of any failure affecting the operation of lamp concealment device(s), lamps shall remain in the position of use if already in use, or shall be capable of being moved into the position of use without tools (applies only if a concealment device were fitted).

Where lamps are concealable, it shall be possible to move them into the position of use and switch them ON by a single control, without excluding moving them into the position of use without switching ON; for grouped main-beam and dipped-beam headlamps the control is required only to activate the dipped-beam headlamps.

Where lamps are concealable, it shall not be possible deliberately, from the driver's seat, to stop the movement of switched ON lamps before they reach the position of use; if there is a danger of dazzling other road users by the movement, the lamps may light up only when they have reached the position of use.

Where a concealment device is used, when it is at a temperature of -30 °C to +50 °C the headlamps shall be capable of reaching the position of use within three seconds of initial operation of the control.

Colours of emitted light shall be as specified: reversing lamp white; stop lamp red; rear position lamp red; rear retro-reflector (non-triangular or triangular) red; rear fog lamp red; rear registration plate lamp white; direction-indicator and hazard warning amber; parking lamp white at front, red at rear (amber if reciprocally incorporated in side direction-indicator or side-marker lamps); rearmost side-marker lamp amber, or red if grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with the rear position, rear end-outline marker, rear fog or stop lamp, or sharing part of the light emitting surface with the rear retro-reflector; rearmost side retro-reflector amber, or red if grouped or sharing light emitting surface with the rear position, end-outline marker, rear fog, stop lamp, red rearmost side-marker lamp or non-triangular rear retro-reflector; emergency stop signal amber or red; rear-end collision alert signal amber; end-outline marker lamp white at front, red at rear; conspicuity marking red or yellow to the rear (white to rear may be allowed by Contracting Parties); reversing projection white; other listed lamps (headlamps, front fog, front position, DRL, cornering, AFS, courtesy, manoeuvring, answer-back) per their individual specifications.

Number of lamps (UN R48 para 5.16): the rear lamp installation shall comply with the number of lamps specified for each lamp function under the applicable provisions of para 5.16 and its sub-paragraphs.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle (including the rear lamp functions) shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.
Any lamp, including the rear lamp, may be installed on movable components (e.g. a tailgate) only if the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. of UN R48 are fulfilled.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, may be installed on movable components only under the conditions of paragraphs 5.18.1. to 5.18.4. of UN R48.

Rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators and rear retro-reflectors may be installed on movable components only if, at all fixed positions of the movable components, the lamps on the movable components meet all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps.

Where the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector functions on movable components are obtained by an assembly of two lamps marked "D" (see paragraph 2.4.11.1.), only one of the lamps needs to meet the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements for those lamps at all fixed positions of the movable components.

Where additional lamps for the rear position, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector functions are fitted and switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.

Where the rear position lamp, rear direction-indicator or rear retro-reflector functions are obtained by an interdependent lamp system, either (a) a complete system mounted on the moving component(s) shall satisfy paragraph 5.18.1., and additional lamps may be switched ON in any fixed open position provided they satisfy all position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps on the movable component; or (b) if the system is partly on the fixed component and partly on a movable component, then, except for direction indicators, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the Applicant during approval shall meet all position, outwards geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s); inwards geometric visibility is deemed satisfied if the lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for approval at all fixed positions; for direction indicator lamps, the specified interdependent lamp(s) shall meet all position, geometric visibility, photometric and colorimetric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s), which does not apply where additional lamps are switched ON in any fixed open position to fulfil or complete the geometric visibility angle, provided they satisfy all position, photometric and colorimetric requirements applicable to the direction indicator lamps installed on the movable component.
When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them (e.g. the rear lamp) shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and that component is in its normal position(s) of use, the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with UN R48. For dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps this is satisfied if, after moving the component and returning it to the normal position 10 times, no measured angular inclination of the lamp relative to its support differs by more than 0.15 per cent from the average of the 10 values; if this value is exceeded, each limit in paragraph 6.2.6.1.1 shall be modified by the excess to reduce the allowed range of inclinations when checking the vehicle according to Annex 6.

The apparent surface, in the direction of the reference axis, of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component (with or without a light-signalling device on it) in any fixed position different from the normal position of use; a fixed position means the stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not; if this is not practicable, the alternatives in paragraphs 5.21.1 and 5.21.2 apply.

If the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the front/rear position lamps, direction-indicator lamps or retro-reflectors is more than 50 per cent hidden by a movable component in a fixed position other than the normal position of use, additional lamps satisfying all position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for those lamps shall be switched ON (alternative to paragraph 5.21.2).

As the alternative where hiding of no more than 50 per cent is not practicable, a remark in the communication form (item 10.1 of Annex 1) shall inform other Administrations that more than 50 per cent of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis can be hidden by the movable components; and a notice in the vehicle shall inform the user that in certain position(s) of the movable components other road users shall be warned of the vehicle's presence on the road, for example by a warning triangle or other devices according to national requirements.
Paragraph 5.21.2 (communication form remark and in-vehicle user notice) does not apply to retro-reflectors.
With the exception of retro-reflectors, a lamp, even bearing an approval mark, is deemed not present when it cannot be made to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse.

Lamps approved with light source(s) according to UN Regulation No. 37, except where those are used as non-replaceable light sources as defined in paragraph 2.9.1.2, shall be fitted so the light source can be correctly replaced without expert assistance and without special tools other than those provided with the vehicle by the manufacturer; the vehicle manufacturer shall provide a detailed description of the replacement procedure with the vehicle.

Where a light source module includes a holder for an approved replaceable light source according to Regulation No. 37, that light source shall be replaceable as required in paragraph 5.23 (without expert assistance or special tools other than those provided by the manufacturer, with a detailed replacement procedure supplied).

Any temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is allowed only if the replacement function in case of failure is similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate, and the replacement device remains operational in its original safety function; during replacement a dashboard tell-tale (paragraph 2.3.5 of UN R48) shall indicate that a temporary replacement has occurred and that repair is needed.

Where an AFS is fitted, it shall be considered equivalent to a pair of dipped-beam headlamps and, if it provides main-beam function(s), equivalent to a pair of main-beam headlamps (applicable only if an AFS is fitted to the vehicle).

Rear direction indicator lamps of category 2b, rear position lamps of category R2 and stop lamps of category S2 with variable luminous intensity control responding simultaneously to one or more conditions in paragraphs 5.26.1 and 5.26.2 are allowed provided that: (a) the intensity of all these lamps, when combined, grouped or reciprocally incorporated, varies all together in the same manner and in a similar proportion; (b) over the entire intensity range, any specific prescribed ratio between the luminous intensities of two lamps is maintained throughout variation transitions.

For variable intensity control of category 2b rear direction indicator, R2 rear position and S2 stop lamps, increase and decrease of luminous intensity, within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations, is allowed in relation to environmental conditions: (a) ambient lighting, (b) fog, (c) snowfall, (d) rain, (e) spray, (f) dust clouds, (g) contamination of the light emitting surface.

For variable intensity control of category 2b, R2 and S2 lamps, independent of the environmental conditions in 5.26.1, a decrease of luminous intensity within the limits prescribed in the pertinent UN Regulations is allowed as long as vehicle speed is equal to or less than 20 km/h or the distance to the following vehicle is equal to or less than 20 m; as long as vehicle speed is equal to or less than 50 km/h, an intensity decrease already activated may remain active.
Stop lamps of category S4 and rear fog lamps of category F2 may produce variable luminous intensity based on the conditions listed in paragraphs 5.26.1 and 5.26.2, independently from the other lamps.

For variable luminous intensity control, no sharp variation of intensity shall be observed during transition; it may be possible for the driver to set the functions concerned to static luminous intensities.

For vehicles of categories M and N, the applicant shall demonstrate to the Technical Service responsible for type approval testing that the electric power supply conditions for the devices indicated in paragraphs 2.5.1, 2.5.2, 2.5.4, 2.5.6 and 2.5.7 comply, with the vehicle electrical system in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the relevant category of powered vehicle as specified by the applicant, with the provisions that follow.

For M and N category vehicles, where the vehicle electrical system is in a constant voltage operating condition representative for the category as specified by the applicant, the voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which according to their type approval documentation were tested with a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, in a secondary operating mode, or at a voltage requested by the applicant shall not exceed the voltage specified for those devices or functions as approved (applicant shall demonstrate this to the Technical Service for devices in 2.5.1., 2.5.2., 2.5.4., 2.5.6. and 2.5.7.).

For M and N category vehicles, in all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by paragraph 5.27.1., the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) by more than 3 per cent; the means of controlling the maximum voltage at the terminals may, for convenience, be located within the body of the device.

The provisions of paragraphs 5.27.1. and 5.27.2. (terminal voltage limits) shall not apply to devices which include an electronic light source control gear, or a variable intensity control being part of the device, or only light source(s) approved according to UN Regulation No. 128.
A report describing the methods used to demonstrate compliance with the electric power supply conditions of paragraph 5.27 and the results obtained shall be attached to the approval documentation.
The general provisions relating to geometric visibility set out in paragraph 5.28 shall be complied with.

There shall be no obstacle inside the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity; obstacles that were already present when the lamp was type-approved are not taken into account.
If geometric visibility measurements are taken closer to the lamp than infinity, the direction of observation shall be shifted parallel in order to achieve the same accuracy.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of its apparent surface is hidden by further parts of the vehicle, proof shall be furnished that the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles still conforms to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

Where the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp mounted less than 750 mm above the ground, measured per paragraph 5.8.1), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.
For an interdependent lamp system, the geometric visibility requirements shall be fulfilled when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
A LED module need not be replaceable if this is stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.

All lamps (devices) installed on the vehicle shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN R48.
In case a light-signalling lamp incorporates a manufacturer logo, the lamp shall be type approved according to the requirements of UN Regulation No. 148.

Lamps installed on a vehicle approved for one or more replaceable light source categories according to Regulations Nos. 37, 99 or 128 shall be fitted only with light sources approved according to those categories; this does not apply to light source modules, LED modules and non-replaceable light sources, except where they are required to be approved by the applicable Regulation.

If an external status indicator for Vehicle Alarm System (VAS), Alarm System (AS) or immobilizer is fitted, one is allowed provided light intensity in any direction does not exceed 0.5 cd, emitted colour is white, red or amber, and apparent surface area is not larger than 20 cm²; up to two such indicators are allowed on a vehicle provided the apparent surface does not exceed 10 cm² per indicator.

A device type approved to any preceding series of amendments to UN Regulations Nos. 148, 149 and/or 150 is deemed equivalent to one approved to the latest series when the change indexes (paragraph 2.1.6) for each individual lamp (function) do not differ; such a device may be fitted on the vehicle to be type approved without update of device type approval documents and markings.

Lamps approved for and equipped with LED substitute light source(s) may be used only where the statement in paragraph 3.2.8 is present and positive; at type approval and in conformity of production verification, the presence of the marking on the lamps related to the use of LED substitute light source(s) shall be checked.
If the vehicle has a Driver Assistance Projection, it shall be constituted of patterns, symbols or both.

If the vehicle has a Driver Assistance Projection, its symbols and patterns shall be related and limited only to warning/highlighting: (a) the presence of a hazardous traffic situation; (b) the presence of other road users which require the driver's attention; (c) maintaining distances to surrounding road users and infrastructure; (d) maintaining the correct lane; the patterns and symbols shall be explained in the owner's handbook.

If front fog lamps are fitted, it shall be possible to switch them ON and OFF independently of the main-beam headlamps, dipped-beam headlamps or any combination of them, unless: (a) the front fog lamps are used as part of another lighting function in an AFS, in which case switching ON the front fog lamps function shall have priority over the function of which they are a part; or (b) the front fog lamps cannot be simultaneously lit with any other lamps with which they are reciprocally incorporated, as indicated by the symbol "/" according to paragraph 10.1 of Annex 1 of UN Regulation No. 19 or item 9.5.1 of Annex 1 of UN Regulation No. [RID].
If front fog lamps are fitted, a closed-circuit tell-tale for them is mandatory.

If front fog lamps are fitted and the communication form of UN Regulation No. 19 or 149 (Annex 1) gives a positive indication under "Luminous intensity is variable", the alignment and luminous intensities of the front fog beam may be automatically adapted to the prevailing ambient conditions; any variation of luminous intensity or alignment shall be performed automatically and in such a way that no discomfort is caused to the driver or other road users.
The reversing lamp shall comply with the individual specifications of UN R48 paragraph 6.4 (heading for the reversing lamp requirements).
The reversing lamp is mandatory on motor vehicles (including M1 passenger cars) and on trailers of categories O2, O3 and O4, and optional on trailers of category O1.
Reversing lamp (UN R48 para 6.4): the number of reversing lamp devices fitted to the vehicle shall comply with the provisions of para 6.4.2 and its sub-clauses.

Reversing lamp number: on motor vehicles of category M1 and on all other vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm, one reversing lamp device shall be fitted (mandatory) and a second device is optional.

Reversing lamp number: on all vehicles with a length exceeding 6,000 mm, except vehicles of category M1, two reversing lamp devices shall be fitted (mandatory) and two additional devices are optional.
Reversing lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Reversing lamp arrangement (para 6.4.3): no special requirement applies to the arrangement of the reversing lamp.
Reversing lamp position (para 6.4.4): the reversing lamp shall be positioned on the vehicle in accordance with the width and height requirements of para 6.4.4.1 and 6.4.4.2.
Reversing lamp position in width: no special requirement applies.

Reversing lamp position in height: the lamp shall be mounted not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground; for off-road vehicles of category N2G, N3G, M2G and M3G the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm.

Reversing lamp position in length: the reversing lamp shall be installed at the rear of the vehicle; however, if installed, the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2 may be fitted on the side of the vehicle, provided that the requirements of paragraphs 6.4.5.2 and 6.4.6.2 are fulfilled.
The reversing lamp shall comply with the geometric visibility requirements specified in paragraph 6.4.5 and its sub-paragraphs.

For reversing lamp devices installed at the rear of the vehicle, geometric visibility, defined by angles α and β as specified in paragraph 2.10.7, shall be: α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards; β = 45° to right and to left if there is only one device, or 45° outwards and 30° inwards if there are two devices.

For the two optional reversing devices of paragraph 6.4.2.2 if fitted on the side of the vehicle, geometric visibility is considered ensured if the reference axis of the respective device is directed outwards with an angle β not exceeding 15° relative to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle; the vertical aim of these two optional devices may be directed downwards.
The reversing lamp shall comply with the orientation requirements specified in paragraph 6.4.6 and its sub-paragraphs.
The reversing lamp shall be oriented rearwards.
In addition, if the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2 are fitted on the side of the vehicle, the provisions of paragraph 6.4.5.2 shall apply to their orientation.
The reversing lamp shall comply with the electrical connection requirements specified in paragraph 6.4.7 of UN R48.

Reversing lamp electrical connections (UN R48 6.4.7.1): the lamp shall be switchable ON only if reverse gear is engaged and the device controlling starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in a position where operation of the propulsion system is possible; it shall not switch ON or remain ON if either condition is not satisfied.

Electrical connections of the two optional devices referred to in paragraph 6.4.2.2 shall ensure they cannot be switched ON unless the lamps referred to in paragraph 5.11 are switched ON; devices fitted on the vehicle side may be switched ON for slow forward manoeuvres up to a maximum of 15 km/h, provided that: (a) they are switched ON and OFF manually by a separate control; (b) if so switched ON, they may remain ON after reverse gear is disengaged; (c) they are automatically switched OFF if forward speed exceeds 15 km/h regardless of the separate control position, and remain OFF until deliberately switched ON again.
Reversing lamp tell-tale (UN R48 6.4.8): a tell-tale is optional, but a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component regulation.
Reversing lamp (UN R48 6.4.9): no other requirements apply.

Section heading for UN R48 6.5 Direction-indicator lamp under individual specifications: the requirements of paragraph 6.5 apply only if a direction-indicator lamp function is fitted in the rear lamp (not listed for this product).

Presence of direction-indicator lamps is mandatory on the vehicle (applies to this rear lamp only if it incorporates the function); types fall into categories 1, 1a, 1b, 2a, 2b, 5 and 6, whose assembly on one vehicle constitutes arrangement A or B; arrangement A shall apply to all motor vehicles; arrangement B shall apply to trailers only.

Number of direction-indicator lamps shall be according to the arrangement; the devices shall be type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 6, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148 (applies if a direction-indicator function is incorporated).

Direction-indicator arrangements (if fitted): Arrangement A: two front lamps of category 1, 1a or 1b depending on the distance between the apparent surface edges and dipped-beam headlamp/front fog lamp (category 1, 1a or 1b if at least 40 mm; 1a or 1b if greater than 20 mm and less than 40 mm; 1b if 20 mm or less); two rear lamps (category 2a or 2b); two optional category 2a or 2b lamps on M2, M3, N2, N3; two side lamps of category 5 or 6 as minimum (category 5 for all M1 and for N1, M2, M3 not exceeding 6 m in length; category 6 for N2, N3 and for N1, M2, M3 exceeding 6 m); category 6 may replace category 5 in all instances; where lamps combine front and side direction-indicator functions, two additional side lamps (category 5 or 6) may be fitted to meet the visibility requirements of paragraph 6.5.5. Arrangement B: two rear lamps (category 2a or 2b); two optional 2a or 2b lamps on O2, O3, O4; maximum three optional category 5 or one optional category 6 device per side on O2 vehicles exceeding 9 m in length. Where an AFS is fitted, the distance for category choice is between the front direction-indicator lamp and the closest lighting unit in its closest position contributing to or performing a passing-beam mode.
Hazard warning signal lamps, as to position height (UN R48 para 6.6.4.2), shall comply with the height requirements specified in paragraph 6.5.4.2.
Hazard warning signal lamps, as to position length (UN R48 para 6.6.4.3), shall comply with the length requirements specified in paragraph 6.5.4.3.
The geometric visibility of the hazard warning signal shall comply with the requirements specified in paragraph 6.5.5.
The orientation of the hazard warning signal lamps shall comply with the requirements specified in paragraph 6.5.6.
The electrical connections of the hazard warning signal shall comply with the requirements of paragraphs 6.6.7.1 to 6.6.7.3.
The hazard warning signal shall be operated by means of a separate manual control enabling all the direction-indicator lamps to flash in phase.

The hazard warning signal may be switched ON automatically if the vehicle is involved in a collision or after the emergency stop signal has been switched OFF (as specified in paragraph 6.23), in which case it may be switched OFF manually; it may also be switched ON automatically to indicate to other road-users the risk of imminent danger as defined by Regulations, in which case the signal shall remain ON until manually or automatically switched OFF.

On M1 and N1 vehicles less than 6 m in length with an arrangement complying with paragraph 6.5.5.2, the amber side-marker lamps, when mounted, shall also flash at the same frequency and in phase with the direction-indicator lamps.
Hazard warning signal (UN R48 para 6.6): a flashing closed-circuit tell-tale shall be provided and is mandatory.

Hazard warning signal other requirements: shall comply with the requirements specified in paragraph 6.5.9; if a power-driven vehicle is equipped to draw a trailer, the hazard warning signal control shall also be capable of bringing the trailer's direction-indicator lamps into action; the hazard warning signal shall be able to function even if the device which starts or stops the propulsion system is in a position which makes it impossible to start the propulsion system.
Stop lamp: the individual specifications of paragraph 6.7 of UN R48 (presence, number, arrangement) shall be met by the stop lamp function of the rear lamp.

Stop lamp presence: devices of S1 or S2 categories are mandatory on all categories of vehicles; devices of S3 or S4 category are mandatory on M1 and N1 vehicles, except chassis-cabs and N1 vehicles with open cargo space, and optional on other vehicle categories.

Stop lamp number: two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device shall be fitted on all categories of vehicles; the devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

Except where a category S3 or S4 device is installed, two optional category S1 or S2 devices may be installed on vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2, N3, O2, O3 and O4 (additional to the two S1 or S2 devices required under 6.7.2).

Only when the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle is not located on a fixed body panel but separates one or two movable parts (e.g. doors) and lacks sufficient space for a single S3 or S4 device on the median longitudinal plane above such movable parts, either two S3 or S4 category type "D" devices may be installed; or one S3 or S4 device may be installed offset to the left or right of the median longitudinal plane; or an interdependent lamp system of category S3 or S4 may be installed.
Stop lamp arrangement: no special requirement applies to the arrangement of the stop lamp.
The position of the stop lamp installed on the vehicle shall comply with UN R48 paragraph 6.7.4 (width, height and length provisions).

Stop lamp position in width: for M1 and N1 vehicles with S1 or S2 category devices, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle, with no special requirement for the distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes; for all other vehicle categories with S1 or S2 devices, the distance between the inner edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall be not less than 600 mm, reducible to 400 mm if the vehicle overall width is less than 1,300 mm; for S3 or S4 devices, the centre of reference shall be on the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, but where two S3 or S4 devices are installed per paragraph 6.7.2 they shall be as close as possible to the median longitudinal plane, one on each side; where one offset S3 or S4 lamp is permitted per paragraph 6.7.2, the offset shall not exceed 150 mm from the median longitudinal plane to the centre of reference of the lamp.
The height of the stop lamp installation shall comply with the provisions of paragraphs 6.7.4.2.1 (S1 or S2) and 6.7.4.2.2 (S3 or S4).

For S1 or S2 stop lamps, the height above the ground shall be not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the bodywork shape makes it impossible to stay within 1,500 mm and optional lamps are not installed); if optional lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a height compatible with the width and symmetry requirements, at a vertical distance as large as the bodywork shape allows, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

For S3 or S4 stop lamps, the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the apparent surface shall either be not more than 150 mm below the horizontal plane tangential to the lower edge of the exposed surface of the glass or glazing of the rear window, or be not less than 850 mm above the ground; in addition, that plane shall be above the horizontal plane tangential to the upper edge of the apparent surface of the S1 or S2 devices.
The stop lamp position in length shall comply with the provisions of paragraphs 6.7.4.4 and 6.7.4.5.
S1 or S2 category stop lamps shall be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.
For S3 or S4 category stop lamps there is no special requirement for the position in length.

Stop lamp geometric visibility: for S1 or S2 devices, horizontal angle 45° to the left and right of the vehicle longitudinal axis, except that for S1/S2 stop lamps mounted below 750 mm (measured per para 5.8.1) the inward 45° angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane; for S3 or S4 devices, 10° left and right of the longitudinal axis. Vertical angle: for S1 or S2, 15° above and below the horizontal, except (a) where mounted below 750 mm (per 5.8.1) the downward 15° may be reduced to 5°, and (b) where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (per 5.8.1) the upward 15° may be reduced to 5°; for S3 or S4, 10° above and 5° below the horizontal.
The stop lamp shall be oriented towards the rear of the vehicle.
The electrical connections of the stop lamp shall comply with paragraphs 6.7.7.1 and 6.7.7.2.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The stop lamps need not function if the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is in a position that makes it impossible for the propulsion system to operate.
A stop lamp tell-tale is optional, but a tell-tale indicating failure shall be provided if required by the component regulation.
The stop lamp shall comply with the other requirements of paragraph 6.7.9, including paragraph 6.7.9.1.
A stop lamp of category S3 or S4 shall not be reciprocally incorporated with any other lamp.
Where an S3 or S4 category device (high-mounted stop lamp) is fitted, it may be installed either outside or inside the vehicle.

If the S3 or S4 category device is installed inside the vehicle, the light it emits shall not cause discomfort to the driver through the devices for indirect vision and/or other surfaces of the vehicle (e.g. the rear window).
Rear registration plate lamp: the individual specifications of UN R48 paragraph 6.8 (presence, number, arrangement, position) shall be met, if a rear registration plate lamp is fitted.
Presence of the rear registration plate lamp is mandatory on the vehicle.

The number of rear registration plate lamp devices shall be such that they illuminate the site of the registration plate according to the type-approval documentation of the device; the devices shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 4, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The arrangement of the rear registration plate lamp shall be such that the device illuminates the site of the registration plate according to the type-approval documentation of the device.
The position of the rear registration plate lamp shall comply with the position requirements of UN R48 paragraph 6.8.4 (heading only, no further values stated in this clause).

If one or more infrared radiation generators are installed inside the front position lamp, they may be switched ON only when the headlamp on the same side of the vehicle is switched ON and the vehicle is in forward motion; if the front position lamp or the headlamp on the same side fails, the infrared radiation generator(s) shall be automatically switched OFF.

In case an AFS providing a bending mode is installed on the vehicle, the front position lamp may be swivelled together with a lighting unit to which it is reciprocally incorporated (UN R48 para 6.9.9.2, other requirements); this applies to the rear lamp only if such an AFS and front position lamp are present.
The rear position lamp shall comply with the individual specifications of UN R48 para 6.10 (presence, number, arrangement, position and related provisions for rear position lamps).
Presence: a rear position lamp of category R, R1 or R2 is mandatory on the vehicle.

Number: two rear position lamps shall be fitted, type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
Except where end-outline marker lamps are installed, two optional additional position lamps may be installed on vehicles of categories M2, M3, N2, N3, O2, O3 and O4 (not applicable to M1 vehicles).
Arrangement of the rear position lamp: no special requirement.
The position of the rear position lamp shall comply with the provisions of UN R48 para 6.10.4 (in width and further position requirements).

In width: the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle (this condition does not apply to the optional rear lamps); the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes: for M1 and N1 vehicles no special requirement; for all other categories not less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall vehicle width is less than 1,300 mm.

Rear position lamp (UN R48 6.10.4.2), position in height: the lamp shall be mounted at a height above the ground of not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed); if the optional lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the requirements of paragraph 6.10.4.1, the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the bodywork shape makes possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
Rear position lamp (UN R48 6.10.4.3), position in length: the lamp shall be mounted at the rear of the vehicle.
Rear position lamp (UN R48 6.10.5): the lamp shall comply with the geometric visibility requirements specified in paragraph 6.10.5 and its sub-paragraphs.

Rear position lamp geometric visibility (UN R48 6.10.5.1): horizontal angle 45° inwards and 80° outwards, where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured per paragraph 5.8.1) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane; vertical angle 15° above and below the horizontal, except (a) where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured per 5.8.1) the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°, and (b) where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured per 5.8.1) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

Rear position lamp alternative geometric visibility (UN R48 6.10.5.2): for M1 and N1 vehicles, as an alternative to 6.10.5.1, at the manufacturer's or accredited representative's discretion and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed, horizontal angle 45° outwards to 45° inwards (inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane if the lamp is mounted below 750 mm, measured per 5.8.1); vertical angle 15° above and below the horizontal (downward angle may be reduced to 5° if mounted below 750 mm, measured per 5.8.1); to be considered visible, the lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 cm²; the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light shall be excluded.
Rear position lamp orientation (UN R48 6.10.6): the lamp shall be oriented rearwards.

Rear position lamp electrical connections (UN R48 6.10.7): the connections shall be in accordance with paragraph 5.11; however, if a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator, the electrical connection of the rear position lamp on the relevant side of the vehicle, or the reciprocally incorporated part of it, may be such that it is switched OFF during the entire time (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the direction-indicator lamp.

Rear position lamp tell-tale (UN R48 6.10.8): a closed-circuit tell-tale is mandatory and shall be combined with that of the front position lamps; this does not apply when daytime running lamps are switched ON; however, a tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
Rear position lamp (UN R48 para 6.10.9, Other requirements): no other requirements apply; none are specified for the rear position lamp beyond those in the preceding paragraphs of 6.10.

Rear fog lamp (UN R48 para 6.11, heading of the individual specifications): where a rear fog lamp is fitted, it shall meet the specifications of paragraphs 6.11.1 to 6.11.4 and subparagraphs (presence, number, arrangement, position). The product spec does not list a rear fog lamp function, so this applies only if one is incorporated.

Rear fog lamp presence (UN R48 para 6.11.1): devices of category F, F1 or F2 are mandatory on the vehicle. This applies to the product only if a rear fog lamp function is used or incorporated in the rear lamp.

Rear fog lamp number (UN R48 para 6.11.2): one or two rear fog lamps shall be fitted, type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 38, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148. This applies if a rear fog lamp is incorporated.
Rear fog lamp arrangement (UN R48 para 6.11.3): no special requirement applies to the arrangement of the rear fog lamp, if one is incorporated.
Rear fog lamp position (UN R48 para 6.11.4, heading): the rear fog lamp, if fitted, shall be positioned in accordance with the width requirement of 6.11.4.1 and the height requirement of 6.11.4.2.

Rear fog lamp position in width (UN R48 para 6.11.4.1): if there is only one rear fog lamp, it shall be on the opposite side of the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle to the direction of traffic prescribed in the country of registration; the centre of reference may also be situated on the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle. Applies if a rear fog lamp is incorporated.

Rear fog lamp position in height (UN R48 para 6.11.4.2): the rear fog lamp shall be not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,000 mm above the ground; for rear fog lamps grouped with any rear lamp the maximum height may be increased to 1,200 mm; for categories N2G, N3G, M2G, M3G (off-road) vehicles the maximum height may be increased to 1,400 mm. Applies if a rear fog lamp is incorporated.

End-outline marker lamp (para 6.13.9), other requirements: provided all other requirements are met, the mandatory or optional lamps visible from the front and those visible from the rear on the same side of the vehicle may be combined into one device; two of the lamps visible from the rear may be grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated in accordance with paragraph 5.7; the position of an end-outline marker lamp relative to the corresponding position lamp shall be such that the distance between the projections on a transverse vertical plane of the nearest points on the apparent surfaces in the direction of the respective reference axes is not less than 200 mm; additional lamps specified in paragraph 6.13.2(a) used to mark the rear end outline of the vehicle, trailer or semi-trailer shall be fitted so as to be visible within the fields of vision of the approved main rear-view devices for indirect vision.

Rear retro-reflector, non-triangular (para 6.14): the individual specifications of paragraphs 6.14.1 to 6.14.4 (presence, number, arrangement, position) shall be met by the rear retro-reflector of the lamp.

Presence of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector: it is mandatory on motor vehicles (including M1); on trailers it is optional provided it is grouped together with the other rear light-signalling devices.

Number of non-triangular rear retro-reflectors: two, type-approved as Class IA or IB retro-reflectors according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150; additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.14.4) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
Arrangement of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector: no special requirement.
Position of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall comply with the requirements of paragraphs 6.14.4.1 (width) and 6.14.4.2 (height).

Position in width of the rear retro-reflector: the point on the illuminating surface farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes has no special requirement for M1 and N1 vehicles; for all other categories it shall be not less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall vehicle width is less than 1,300 mm.

Position in height of the rear retro-reflector: above the ground not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm; not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s); up to 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively.
For the non-triangular rear retro-reflector (UN R48 6.14), its position in length shall be at the rear of the vehicle.

The non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall have geometric visibility with a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and outwards and a vertical angle of 10° above and below horizontal; where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
The non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be oriented rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the non-triangular rear retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.
Heading for UN R48 paragraph 6.15 (Rear retro-reflector, triangular): the requirements of paragraphs 6.15.1 to 6.15.3 apply to triangular rear retro-reflectors.
Triangular rear retro-reflectors are mandatory on trailers and prohibited on motor vehicles; therefore the M1 passenger car rear lamp shall not include a triangular rear retro-reflector.

Where triangular rear retro-reflectors are fitted (trailers), there shall be two, type-approved as Class IIIA or Class IIIB retro-reflectors under the 02 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or the 00 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150; additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.15.4) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
Where a triangular rear retro-reflector is fitted (trailers), the apex of the triangle shall be directed upwards.
The position of the triangular rear retro-reflector (UN R48 para 6.15) shall comply with the position requirements of para 6.15.4 on width, height and length.

Triangular rear retro-reflector position in width: the point on the illuminating surface farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; the inner edges of the retro-reflectors shall be not less than 600 mm apart, a distance which may be reduced to 400 mm if the overall width of the vehicle is less than 1,300 mm.

Triangular rear retro-reflector position in height: above the ground not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm; not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s); up to 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively.
Triangular rear retro-reflector position in length: it shall be located at the rear of the vehicle.

Geometric visibility of the triangular rear retro-reflector: horizontal angle 30° inwards and outwards; vertical angle 15° above and below the horizontal; where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured per para 5.8.1), the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
The triangular rear retro-reflector shall be oriented rearwards.
The illuminating surface of the triangular rear retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the rear.

Heading of UN R48 para 6.16 under individual specifications: front retro-reflector, non-triangular; its specific requirements apply only if such a front retro-reflector is fitted, which is not a function of this rear lamp.

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular (UN R48 para 6.16.1, Presence): shall be fitted where mandatory, i.e. mandatory on trailers and on motor vehicles having all forward facing lamps with reflectors concealable; optional on other motor vehicles.

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular (Number): two shall be fitted, type-approved as Class IA or IB retro-reflectors under the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150; additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.16.4) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
Front retro-reflector, non-triangular (Arrangement): no special requirement applies to the arrangement.
Front retro-reflector, non-triangular: the position shall comply with the width, height and length requirements of paragraph 6.16.4 (6.16.4.1 to 6.16.4.3).

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular, position in width: the point of the illuminating surface farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; for a trailer, not farther than 150 mm from the extreme outer edge; the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall have no special requirement for M1 and N1 vehicles, and for all other categories be not less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall vehicle width is less than 1,300 mm.

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular, position in height: above the ground, not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm (1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm).
Front retro-reflector, non-triangular, position in length: it shall be located at the front of the vehicle.

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular, geometric visibility: horizontal angle 30° inwards and outwards (for trailers the inward angle may be reduced to 10°; if trailer construction prevents the mandatory retro-reflectors meeting this angle, additional supplementary retro-reflectors shall be fitted, without the width limitation of 6.16.4.1, which together with the mandatory ones give the necessary visibility angle); vertical angle 10° above and below the horizontal, where the downward angle may be reduced to 5° if the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured per paragraph 5.8.1).
Front retro-reflector, non-triangular (UN R48 para 6.16.6): the orientation of the retro-reflector shall be towards the front.

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular (UN R48 para 6.16.7), other requirements: the illuminating surface of the retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp situated at the front.
Individual specifications (UN R48 para 6.17): side retro-reflector, non-triangular; the requirements of paragraphs 6.17.1 to 6.17.4 apply to it.

Side retro-reflector, non-triangular, presence (UN R48 para 6.17.1): mandatory on all motor vehicles the length of which exceeds 6 m and on all trailers; optional on motor vehicles the length of which does not exceed 6 m.

Side retro-reflector, non-triangular, number (UN R48 para 6.17.2): the number shall be such that the requirements for longitudinal positioning are complied with; the devices shall be type-approved as Class IA or IB retro-reflectors under the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150; additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.17.4) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
Side retro-reflector, non-triangular, arrangement (UN R48 para 6.17.3): no special requirement.
Side retro-reflector, non-triangular, position (UN R48 para 6.17.4): the position shall comply with the requirements of the sub-paragraphs of 6.17.4, including paragraph 6.17.4.1 on width.
Side retro-reflector, non-triangular, position in width (UN R48 para 6.17.4.1): no special requirement.

Side retro-reflector, non-triangular (UN R48 6.17.4.2) position in height: mount it above the ground not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm; up to 1,200 mm if grouped with any lamp(s); up to 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively, or if the presence of the device is not mandatory according to paragraph 6.17.1.

Side retro-reflector, non-triangular (UN R48 6.17.4.3) position in length: fit at least one side retro-reflector in the middle third of the vehicle, with the foremost one not further than 3 m (4 m for semi-trailers) from the front; the distance between adjacent side retro-reflectors shall not exceed 3 m (this does not apply to M1 and N1 vehicles; it may be increased to 4 m if structure, design or operational use makes compliance impossible); the distance from the rearmost side retro-reflector to the rear shall not exceed 1 m; for motor vehicles not longer than 6 m, one side retro-reflector within the first third and/or one within the last third of the vehicle length is sufficient; for M1 vehicles longer than 6 m but not longer than 7 m, one side retro-reflector not further than 3 m from the front and one within the last third of the vehicle length is sufficient.

Side retro-reflector, non-triangular (UN R48 6.17.5) geometric visibility: horizontal angle 45° to the front and to the rear; vertical angle 10° above and below the horizontal; where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1), the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
Side retro-reflector, non-triangular (UN R48 6.17.6) orientation: the side retro-reflector shall be oriented towards the side.

Side retro-reflector, non-triangular (UN R48 6.17.7) other requirements: the illuminating surface of the side retro-reflector may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other side lamp.
Individual specifications (UN R48 6.18): side-marker lamps shall comply with the requirements of paragraph 6.18 and its subparagraphs, where such lamps are fitted.

Side-marker lamps presence (UN R48 6.18.1): mandatory on all vehicles longer than 6 m, except chassis-cabs; the SM1 type shall be used on all vehicle categories, while SM2 type may be used on M1; on M1 and N1 vehicles less than 6 m long, side-marker lamps shall be used if they supplement the reduced geometric visibility of front position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.9.5.2 and rear position lamps conforming to paragraph 6.10.5.2; optional on all other vehicles, where SM1 or SM2 types may be used.

Daytime running lamps electrical connections (UN R48 6.19.7.1): switch the daytime running lamps ON automatically when the device that starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position allowing the propulsion system to operate, unless any of the following exists: (a) front fog lamps are switched ON; (b) headlamps are manually switched ON, except when used for intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals; (c) conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

Irrespective of paragraphs 6.19.7.1 and 6.19.7.5 of UN R48, where conditions require daytime running lamps to be ON, they may remain OFF, or once automatically switched ON may be manually switched OFF and remain OFF, while at least one of the following conditions exists: (a) automatic transmission control is in park position; (b) parking brake is in locked position; (c) prior to the vehicle being set in motion for the first time after each manual activation of the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system; (d) vehicle speed does not exceed 15 km/h.

Automatic operation of the daytime running lamps shall be resumed as soon as the conditions described in paragraph 6.19.7.2 of UN R48 (park position, parking brake locked, before first movement after propulsion start/stop activation, speed not above 15 km/h) no longer exist.

The daytime running lamp shall switch OFF automatically when the device which starts and/or stops the propulsion system is set in a position making propulsion operation impossible, and when any of the following exists: (a) front fog lamps are switched ON; (b) headlamps are manually switched ON, except when used for intermittent luminous warnings at short intervals; (c) conditions of Annex 13 for automatic switching ON of dipped-beam headlamps exist.

When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON; other lamps mentioned in paragraph 5.11 may also be switched ON. However, the rear position lamps and the other lamps of paragraph 5.11 may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are ON, and may remain OFF as long as ambient light outside the vehicle is above 7,000 lux (measured according to Annex 13).

If a front direction-indicator lamp is not reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp and the distance between the edges of their apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the direction-indicator lamp is 40 mm or less, the DRL electrical connections shall be such that either (a) the DRL on the relevant side is switched OFF during the entire period (ON and OFF cycle) of direction-indicator operation; or (b) the DRL luminous intensity on that side is reduced during the entire period to not more than 140 cd within the angles of geometric visibility. Conformity shall be verified at DRL type approval and indicated in the communication form. If the direction-indicator luminous intensity in HV is at least 50% higher than the DRL intensity in HV, the DRL need not be switched OFF or dimmed, and the applicant shall demonstrate compliance with a concise description or other means acceptable to the Type Approval Authority.

If a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp, the electrical connection requirements of paragraph 6.19.7.7.1 or the alternative following it shall be met (introductory clause).

Where a front direction-indicator lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a daytime running lamp having totally common apparent surfaces, the electrical connections shall be such that the daytime running lamp function on the relevant side of the vehicle is switched OFF during the entire period (both ON and OFF cycle) of operation of the front direction-indicator lamp, or the alternative provision that follows is met.

Conspicuity markings shall be considered continuous if the distance between adjacent elements is as small as possible and does not exceed 50 per cent of the shortest adjacent element length; if the manufacturer proves to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority that 50 per cent cannot be respected, the distance may be larger but shall be as small as possible and not exceed 1,000 mm.

UN R48 6.21.7.2 (Other requirements, conspicuity marking): In the case of a partial contour marking, each upper corner shall be described by two lines at 90° to each other, each at least 250 mm in length; if this is not possible, the marking shall follow as closely as practicable the contour of the outer shape of the vehicle.
UN R48 6.21.7.3 (Other requirements, conspicuity marking): The distance between the conspicuity marking fitted to the rear of a vehicle and each mandatory stop lamp should be greater than 200 mm.

UN R48 6.21.7.4 (Other requirements, conspicuity marking): Where rear marking plates type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 70, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150, are installed, they may be considered, at the manufacturer's discretion, as part of the rear conspicuity marking for calculating the length of the conspicuity marking and its proximity to the side of the vehicle.
UN R48 6.21.7.5 (Other requirements, conspicuity marking): The locations on the vehicle designated for conspicuity markings shall allow installation of markings at least 60 mm in width.

UN R48 6.22 (Individual specifications, Adaptive front lighting system, AFS): Where not otherwise specified in paragraph 6.22, the requirements for main-beam headlamps (paragraph 6.1) and for dipped-beam headlamps (paragraph 6.2) of UN R48 apply to the relevant part of the AFS.
UN R48 6.22.1 (AFS, Presence): An AFS is optional on motor vehicles and is prohibited on trailers.
UN R48 6.22.2 (AFS, Number): Where an AFS is fitted, the number shall be one, type-approved according to the 01 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 149.
UN R48 6.22.3 (AFS, Arrangement): No special requirements apply to the arrangement of the adaptive front lighting system.

For an adaptive front lighting system (AFS), where not otherwise specified in paragraph 6.22, the requirements for main-beam headlamps (6.1) and dipped-beam headlamps (6.2) apply to the relevant part of the AFS; the AFS shall be set to the neutral state prior to the subsequent test procedures.

For the AFS in the neutral state, for a given lighting function or mode, the requirements of paragraphs 6.22.4.1.1 through 6.22.4.1.4 (position in width and height) shall be fulfilled by those lighting units energized simultaneously for that function or mode according to the applicant's description; all dimensions refer to the nearest edge of the apparent surface(s) observed in the direction of the reference axis of the lighting unit(s).

Two symmetrically placed lighting units of the AFS shall be positioned at a height complying with paragraphs 6.1.4 and 6.2.4; they are one on each side of the vehicle with the geometric centres of gravity of their apparent surfaces at the same height and the same distance from the vehicle's longitudinal median plane within a tolerance of 50 mm each; their light emitting surfaces, illuminating surfaces and light outputs may differ.

Additional lighting units, if any, on either side of the vehicle shall be positioned not more than 140 mm horizontally (E in the figure) and not more than 400 mm vertically above or below (D in the figure) from the nearest lighting unit; in case of additional two symmetrically placed lighting units, the horizontal distance may be 200 mm (C in the figure).
The vehicle shall comply with the individual specifications of paragraph 6.23 for the emergency stop signal.

The emergency stop signal is mandatory on motor vehicles and optional on trailers; it shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop lamps or direction-indicator lamps fitted, as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
The number of lamps used for the emergency stop signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.2 (stop lamps) or 6.7.2 (direction-indicator lamps).
The arrangement of lamps used for the emergency stop signal shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.3 (stop lamps) or 6.7.3 (direction-indicator lamps).
Emergency stop signal (UN R48 para 6.23): the position of the lamps shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.4 (stop lamps) or 6.7.4 (direction indicator/hazard warning lamps), as applicable.
Emergency stop signal (UN R48 para 6.23): the geometric visibility shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.5 or 6.7.5, as applicable.
Emergency stop signal (UN R48 para 6.23): the orientation shall be as specified in paragraph 6.5.6 or 6.7.6, as applicable.

Emergency stop signal (UN R48 para 6.23): the electrical connections shall comply with the provisions of paragraphs 6.23.7.1 to 6.23.7.3 (flashing frequency and phase, independent operation, automatic switching ON and OFF).
Electrical connections of the emergency stop signal: all lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.

Electrical connections of the emergency stop signal: if any of the emergency stop signal lamps at the rear of the vehicle use filament light sources, the flashing frequency shall be 4.0 +0.0/-1.0 Hz instead of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
Electrical connections of the emergency stop signal: the emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
Electrical connections of the emergency stop signal: the emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.

Where the vehicle has an emergency stop signal, it shall be switched ON automatically only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.

Where the vehicle has an emergency stop signal, it shall be switched OFF automatically if the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided or if the hazard warning signal is activated.
A tell-tale for the emergency stop signal is optional; if one is fitted, it is subject to the Regulation's provisions for the emergency stop signal tell-tale.
Where the vehicle has an emergency stop signal, the other requirements of paragraph 6.23.9 on towing and trailer operation shall be met.

Except as provided in paragraph 6.23.9.2, if a motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer, its emergency stop signal control shall also operate the trailer's emergency stop signal. When electrically connected to a trailer, the operating frequency for the combination shall be limited to that specified in 6.23.7.1.1; however, if the motor vehicle can detect that filament light sources are not used on the trailer for the emergency stop signal, the frequency may be that specified in 6.23.7.1.

If a motor vehicle is equipped to tow a trailer fitted with a continuous or semi-continuous service braking system as defined in Regulation No. 13, a constant power supply shall be provided via the electrical connector to the trailer's stop lamps while the service brake is applied. The trailer's emergency stop signal may operate independently of the towing vehicle and need not operate at the same frequency or in phase with that of the towing vehicle.

Illuminating surface and light-emitting surface of a single function lamp shall be determined per paragraphs 2.10.2 to 2.10.3 as illustrated in Part 5 examples 1-9: light source with reflector optic, with inner lens or partial inner lens, or light guide optic, behind an outer lens, including or excluding the non-textured outer lens, and in combination with an area not part of the function.

The light-emitting surface shall be determined relative to the illuminating surface per paragraphs 2.8 and 2.9 as illustrated in Part 6 examples A-E (declared light-emitting surface per 2.10.2 (a) with edges; illuminating surface with an area not part of the function; apparent surface with a non-textured outer lens per 2.10.2 (b)); reflected light may contribute to determining the light-emitting surface.

Where two functions are reciprocally incorporated in the lamp, the decision on reciprocal incorporation shall follow the Part 7 examples of UN R48: cases with a textured outer lens (with or without a wall in between), with the non-textured outer lens excluded, or with the outer lens (textured or not) included; where the non-textured outer lens is excluded, "7b" is the apparent surface according to paragraph 2.10.2. and F1 shall not be transparent to F2.

Visibility of a red lamp to the front and of a white lamp to the rear (e.g. the white reversing lamp) shall be assessed per paragraph 5.10.4. using Annex 4 zones 1 and 2, bounded in height by horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground, and in width by vertical planes forming a 15° angle outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane to the front and rear respectively, passing through the contact points of the vertical planes parallel to the median longitudinal plane delimiting the overall width; if there are several contact points, the foremost corresponds to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane.

The position of the lamps as defined in paragraph 2.1.6. shall be checked in width, height and length per the general requirements of paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4.; the measured distances shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
The visibility of the lamps shall be tested as part of the Annex 9 tests (heading for geometric visibility angles and red-to-front/white-to-rear visibility checks).

The angles of geometric visibility shall be checked per paragraph 2.10.7.; measured angles shall fulfil the individual specifications for each lamp, except that the angle limits may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall be checked in accordance with paragraph 5.10.
Heading for the Annex 9 test on alignment of dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps towards the front; it is not applicable to the rear lamp, which has no such functions.

The initial downward inclination of the dipped-beam cut-off and of front fog lamps shall be set to the plated figure required and shown in Annex 7; alternatively, the manufacturer shall set the initial aim to a different figure if it can be shown to be representative of the type approved when tested per Annex 6, in particular paragraph 4.1 (applies only to front lamps, not to this rear lamp).

For the alignment of dipped-beam headlamps and front fog lamps towards the front, the variation of the dipped-beam downward inclination as a function of the loading conditions shall remain within the limits by mounting height h [m]: 0.5 ≤ h ≤ 0.9 upper limit -0.50 per cent and lower limit -(h + 1.2) per cent; 0.9 < h ≤ 1.2 upper limit -(h x 2.17 - 1.45) and lower limit -(h x 2.17 + 0.15) per cent; 1.2 < h ≤ 1.5 as specified in the table. For a front fog lamp with light source(s) of total objective luminous flux exceeding 2,000 lumens, the variation shall remain within: h < 0.8: 0.7 per cent minimum and 3.3 per cent maximum vertical inclination; h > 0.8: 1.2 per cent minimum and 3.8 per cent maximum vertical inclination. The states of loading used shall be those indicated in Annex 5 of this Regulation, for every system adjusted accordingly.

For vehicles of category M1, the variation of inclination with load shall be verified within the limits of Annex 9 paragraph 1.3.2 using the loading conditions of Paragraph 2.1.1.1 and Paragraph 2.1.1.6, taking into account Paragraph 2.1.2.

For vehicles of category M2 and M3, the variation of inclination with load shall be verified within the limits of Annex 9 paragraph 1.3.2 using the loading conditions of Paragraph 2.2.1 and Paragraph 2.2.2.

For vehicles of category N with load surfaces, the variation of inclination with load shall be verified within the limits of Annex 9 paragraph 1.3.2 using the loading conditions of Paragraph 2.3.1.1 and Paragraph 2.3.1.2.

For vehicles of category N without load surfaces, the variation of inclination with load shall be verified within the limits of Annex 9 paragraph 1.3.2 according to the sub-paragraphs for drawing vehicles for semi-trailers (1.3.2.4.1) and for trailers (1.3.2.4.2).

For category N vehicles without load surfaces that are drawing vehicles for semi-trailers, the variation of inclination with load shall be verified within the limits of Annex 9 paragraph 1.3.2 using the loading conditions of Paragraph 2.4.1.1 and Paragraph 2.4.1.2.

For category N vehicles without load surfaces that are drawing vehicles for trailers, the variation of inclination with load shall be verified within the limits of Annex 9 paragraph 1.3.2 using the loading conditions of Paragraph 2.4.2.1 and Paragraph 2.4.2.2.

The electrical connections shall be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle; the lamps and tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions of paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of this Regulation and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.
Annex 9 (Tests), paragraph 1.5: light intensities of the lamps fitted to the vehicle shall be checked in accordance with the following sub-paragraphs of this Regulation.

For main-beam headlamps (applicable only if the vehicle is fitted with them; the rear lamp itself has none), the aggregate maximum intensity shall be checked by the procedure in paragraph 6.1.9.2 of UN R48, and the value obtained shall fulfil the requirement of paragraph 6.1.9.1 of UN R48.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps (including rear position, stop and reversing lamps and the rear retro-reflector) shall be checked by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, and shall be such that the requirements of paragraphs 5.15 and 5.16 of UN R48 and the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
Annex 10 of UN R48 is reserved and contains no technical requirements; no compliance action is required for it.

Annex 11 of UN R48: the visibility of conspicuity markings to the rear, front and side of a vehicle shall be as specified in this annex, in accordance with paragraph 6.21.5 of UN R48 (applicable only if conspicuity markings are fitted).
